Intuit Targets Complex Subscription Billing With Sequence Deal
The QuickBooks parent plans to acquire technology for managing custom contracts and usage-based billing, bringing subscription operations and accounting software closer together.
Intuit, the company behind QuickBooks, announced October 15 that it has agreed to acquire Sequence, a software company that helps businesses manage customer contracts, billing, collections and revenue accounting.
The acquisition would expand Intuit's ability to serve businesses whose revenue doesn't fit neatly into a standard monthly or annual subscription. Sequence handles arrangements involving customer seats, usage charges, minimum spending commitments and individually negotiated terms.
For subscription operators, the news points to a potential shift in the technology market. Large financial software companies are moving further into work traditionally handled by specialized subscription billing and revenue management systems.
A software company might sell annual subscriptions to business customers, with some paying a fixed fee and others paying according to the number of employees using the product. Larger customers may have negotiated agreements that combine minimum commitments with additional usage charges.
When customers add seats, change their usage or renegotiate terms, the billing system has to keep up. The next invoice needs to reflect what was agreed, while finance needs accurate records of what has been billed, collected and earned.
Sequence is designed to handle those different arrangements. Its platform connects customer contracts to billing schedules, calculates charges based on agreed terms, prepares invoices and helps manage collections. It also supports revenue recognition, the accounting process for recording revenue as a company earns it.
Sequence already connects with QuickBooks and other accounting systems. Intuit plans to go further by bringing Sequence's capabilities into its own mid-market products, including Intuit Enterprise Suite and QuickBooks Online Advanced.
The acquisition has not yet closed, and the companies haven't disclosed the purchase price. Intuit says it will continue supporting existing Sequence customers after the deal closes and plans to develop an integrated offering in the coming months. Future product pricing and availability haven't been announced.
Sequence uses AI agents to help finance teams with work that often requires manual attention. Its software can read signed contracts, identify pricing terms, prepare billing information and draft reminders for overdue invoices. It can also assist with matching payments to outstanding invoices.
Sequence draws a distinction between what its AI agents do and how customer charges are calculated. The company says AI does not calculate the amounts customers owe. Instead, its billing engine uses defined pricing rules and contract terms to produce charges that can be checked and reproduced. Sequence also describes controls that allow finance teams to review and approve work performed by its AI agents.
For subscription operators, that approach addresses a practical concern. When customers question an invoice, the business needs to explain where the charge came from, particularly when pricing involves changing usage, discounts or adjustments during a contract.
Intuit hasn't yet explained how Sequence's AI capabilities will appear in its own products.
Financial Software Companies Move Further Into Recurring Revenue
Intuit isn't the only major financial technology company expanding into specialized billing technology.
In January, Stripe completed its acquisition of Metronome, which provides technology for managing usage-based, subscription and hybrid billing models. Both acquisitions point to growing interest among larger financial technology companies in the systems businesses use to manage recurring revenue.
Companies with complex pricing often rely on a combination of specialized billing platforms, accounting software and spreadsheets. Keeping customer agreements, invoices and financial records consistent across those systems can take considerable work.
Intuit's move could eventually give companies with complex billing needs another option for managing contracts, charges and financial records within the same platform. Whether that approach is a better fit than a specialized billing provider will depend on the company's pricing arrangements, operating needs and the capabilities of the eventual product.
For years, subscription billing and accounting have been treated as separate jobs. Billing systems manage what customers owe under their subscriptions and contracts. Accounting systems record the financial results. Intuit's planned acquisition of Sequence suggests that separation may be changing.
Stripe's acquisition of Metronome earlier this year points in a similar direction. Large financial technology companies are moving deeper into the systems that manage recurring revenue, an area where specialized subscription billing providers have traditionally played a central role.
For subscription operators, the bigger question is whether billing technology will increasingly become part of a company's broader financial software decision. That could change who chooses the systems, how they work together and how much control subscription teams have over the tools they depend on.
There are potential advantages to bringing billing and accounting closer together, particularly when customer contracts and pricing change frequently. But a financial platform still has to handle the exceptions that make subscription billing difficult. A customer adding seats halfway through a contract or disputing a usage charge needs an accurate answer, regardless of which company supplies the software.
Intuit hasn't said how it will price or package Sequence's capabilities, and the acquisition hasn't closed. We don't yet know whether the combined offering will be a better alternative to established subscription billing platforms. But if accounting platforms begin taking on more responsibility for subscription billing, operators may find that decisions affecting their customer relationships are increasingly tied to choices made elsewhere in the business.
Intuit's planned acquisition of Sequence raises a question for subscription operators: if billing becomes part of a broader financial platform, who makes the technology decisions, and how are the subscription team's needs protected? Intuit (INTU): Can Credit Karma Grow Beyond the Lending Cycle?
Tue, October 20, 2026 at 8:49 AM CDT 4 min read
Intuit Inc. (NASDAQ:INTU), featured among Insider Monkey's 10 Best Software Stocks to Buy in 2026, has a growing financial marketplace inside its software business. Credit Karma revenue rose 20% to $2.64 billion in fiscal 2026. As banks tighten credit-card standards, insurance offers another way to grow. Yet personal loans and credit cards still generated most of the increase.
Intuit Inc. (NASDAQ:INTU) has a 13x forward P/E and an 18x trailing P/E. Trailing P/E uses past earnings, while forward P/E uses forecast earnings. Management separately projects fiscal 2027 GAAP EPS growth of 22%–24%. The forward valuation looks provisionally reasonable if stronger earnings support cash generation after higher tax payments.
The forward P/E was 35x in July 2025. Intuit Inc. (NASDAQ:INTU) now expects revenue growth of 9%–10%, versus 14% last year, supporting a more moderate valuation. Management also now includes stock compensation in adjusted earnings. That makes the distinction between operating progress and accounting adjustments important when assessing its guidance.
H&R Block, Inc. (NYSE:HRB), a close tax-preparation comparison, has a 7x forward P/E. Intuit Inc. (NASDAQ:INTU) guides to non-GAAP EPS growth of 23%–24% under its revised definition for the fiscal year ending July 2027, versus approximately 14%–18% for its rival's June 2027 year. Faster growth and recurring business-software revenue support a premium over a business more dependent on seasonal tax preparation.

TD Cowen Expects Strong Q3 Performance from Intuit (INTU)
From Loan Referrals to a Broader Financial Marketplace
Intuit Inc. (NASDAQ:INTU) added $441 million of Credit Karma revenue last year: $235 million from personal loans, $101 million from credit cards and $85 million from insurance. Lending supplied roughly 76% of incremental revenue; insurance contributed 19%. Diversification is advancing, but borrowing remains the main growth engine.
Intuit Inc. (NASDAQ:INTU) has products designed to encourage visits without another loan application. My Cards helps members manage existing card rewards, while Karma Drive uses driving data to identify insurance discounts. These services could reduce the cost of attracting returning customers and create referral opportunities. The test is whether customer benefits also improve shareholder economics. Revenue from additional visits must exceed product, marketing, and servicing costs.
Consolidated finances give Intuit Inc. (NASDAQ:INTU) room to invest. Fiscal 2026 operating cash flow reached $8.84 billion against $221 million of capital expenditure. It included a $2.06 billion stock-compensation addback. Credit Karma represented roughly 12% of group revenue, leaving accounting and tax products as substantial buffers.
Fiscal 2026 cash generation also benefited from lower cash-tax payments, including deductions for previously capitalized research spending. Management expects approximately $2 billion of cash taxes in fiscal 2027, so stronger operating earnings must help offset that higher cash outflow.
Revenue Diversification Must Survive Tighter Credit
For Intuit Inc. (NASDAQ:INTU), engagement and monetization can move in opposite directions. The Federal Reserve's July survey found tighter credit-card lending standards despite broadly unchanged demand. Credit Karma generally earns card and personal-loan referral fees when cards are issued or loans funded. Fewer approvals can therefore reduce revenue even with steady traffic. Compared with putting customer knowledge to work through direct lending, referrals make partners' willingness to approve and acquire borrowers central to revenue.
Insurance leads provide another revenue source without requiring new borrowing, but insurers can also cut acquisition budgets. Management's 11%–13% Credit Karma growth forecast for fiscal 2027 anticipates moderation. Investors need evidence that insurance revenue, repeat engagement, and conversion improve together. The combined Consumer segment's margin cannot isolate Credit Karma's profitability.
Intuit Inc. (NASDAQ:INTU) looks fairly valued at 13x forward P/E. Sustaining that judgment requires operating profit growth to absorb higher cash taxes while insurance and other services expand their contribution. Resilient referral conversion during tighter credit would strengthen the case for more dependable earnings. Continued dependence on loan growth would leave the diversification thesis unfinished.
While we acknowledge the risk and potential of INTU as an investment, our conviction lies in the belief that some AI stocks hold greater promise for delivering higher returns and doing so within a shorter time frame. Intuit Launches Credit Karma Tax: Free Federal Filing With Faster Refunds, Expanding Its Daily AI-Powered Financial Assistance
Tue, October 20, 2026 at 8:30 AM CDT 5 min read
Combines Free, $0 Federal, and flat-rate, $15* State filing, regardless of your tax complexity, with refunds up to 5 days early for free through Credit Karma
AI-powered support before, during and after tax season, alongside daily financial tools deliver less work, simplified filing and financial confidence to members
MOUNTAIN VIEW, Calif., October 20, 2026--(BUSINESS WIRE)--Intuit Inc. (Nasdaq: INTU), the global financial technology platform that makes TurboTax, Credit Karma, QuickBooks, Mailchimp, Intuit Enterprise Suite, and Intuit Accountant Suite, today announced the launch of Credit Karma Tax offering a simple, flat-rate pricing model of free, $0 federal and flat-rate, $15 state filing to all members, no matter their tax complexity. Credit Karma, a daily financial assistant, combines transparent pricing, faster access to refunds and financial confidence all in one place. With Credit Karma Tax, members get a self-guided DIY experience with real-time AI help that simplifies the process throughout, tackling the majority of the manual work that filing often requires. AI-powered tools support members every step of the way, from giving them a head start by centralizing key financial data, then optimizing tax outcomes as they file, and delivering refunds faster, to building long-term financial health long after they submit their taxes.
"Today Credit Karma is so much more than a place to check your credit score; it's delivering true financial confidence, where daily money management helps build the life our members want whether that's affording a place to call home for their family, or planning a dream trip," said Mark Notarainni, Executive Vice President and General Manager, Consumer Group, Intuit. "By adding transparent, free Federal filing specifically tailored to our members, no matter how complex their tax situation, we are expanding Credit Karma's role as their daily AI-powered financial assistant, helping them strategically spend, save, and grow their money in one place."
Centralized Data Delivers Unmatched Speed and Convenience
Credit Karma is already part of millions of consumers' daily financial routines. By centralizing a member's financial data, including income, credit, cash flow and taxes all in one place, when tax time arrives, Credit Karma members already have a head start. Filers can skip manual data entry by simply snapping a photo or automatically importing forms directly from employers or financial institutions, including stock sales, and financial and crypto transactions. Credit Karma Tax will pre-fill the return, and with its comprehensive document checklist and gathering tools, the guesswork is removed from filing.
File & Achieve Financial Progress with Confidence: Accuracy Guaranteed, AI Assistance, and Refunds Directed Toward Money Goals
From the moment members start filing to the moment their refund lands, Credit Karma Tax utilizes Intuit's domain expertise, AI and platform technology to get it right and make that money work harder for them.
Tax Prep & Filing: Credit Karma Tax provides real-time help, gives clear explanations of return outcomes, and catches errors along the way using built-in AI tools like its expert chat function and, coming soon, Explanation and Error Agents.
Review & Submission: Credit Karma Tax runs thousands of accuracy checks prior to submission to ensure compliance with IRS and state requirements. All returns are backed by a 100% accuracy guarantee. If a calculation error causes an IRS or state penalty, Intuit covers the penalty and interest.
Completion & Refund Acceleration: Credit Karma Tax doesn't stop at filing. Tax refunds are often the single biggest financial event of the year for Americans. Credit Karma transforms that moment into year-round financial health through its suite of AI-powered financial tools. The Refund Agent turns refunds into actionable plans to pay down debt, save, or invest; the Debt Agent builds personalized paydown plans saving members $200+ a month; and the Paycheck Agent allocates paychecks across bills, spending, and goals.
With 70% of Americans relying on tax refunds to cover basic living expenses, for this upcoming tax season Credit Karma Tax provides accelerated access to funds:
Up to 5 Days Early: Access federal tax refunds up to 5 days early for free with deposit into a Credit Karma Checking account.1
Refund Advance Loan: With the upcoming launch of Credit Karma Tax's Tax Year 2026 offering, apply for an up to a $4,000 Refund Advance loan with $0 loan fees and 0% APR.1
Credit Karma Tax offers a predictable, flat-rate pricing structure, regardless of tax complexity, with no hidden fees: $0 Federal Filing, $15 per State Filing.
For filers seeking added peace of mind or expert support as they file their 2026 taxes, Credit Karma Tax offers straightforward paid add-ons:
Expert Support Bundle: Includes audit defense, ID protection benefits, 1:1 live product support, and the ability to pay the $15 state fee using a tax refund. ($29 at launch. Pricing subject to change)¹.
Expert Final Review: An option to add a final review by a tax expert to the above bundle will also be available at launch. ($39 at launch. Pricing subject to change)¹.
Operating as a distinct, streamlined tax preparation offering, Credit Karma Tax is available on the Credit Karma website and app. To become a member and create a free Credit Karma account visit creditkarma.com.

Intuit's financial intelligence brings together decades of trusted data, deep financial expertise, AI, and human experts to help customers at every stage of their financial journey. This puts more money in their pockets, saves time by reducing manual work, and ensures they have complete confidence in every financial decision. For more information, visit Intuit.com.

Wall Street Analysts Think Intuit (INTU) Could Surge 26.36%: Read This Before Placing a Bet
Tue, October 20, 2026 at 7:55 AM CDT 4 min read
Intuit (INTU) closed the last trading session at $325.62, gaining 7.1% over the past four weeks, but there could be plenty of upside left in the stock if short-term price targets set by Wall Street analysts are any guide. The mean price target of $411.45 indicates a 26.4% upside potential.
The average comprises 31 short-term price targets ranging from a low of $290.00 to a high of $900.00, with a standard deviation of $126.65. While the lowest estimate indicates a decline of 10.9% from the current price level, the most optimistic estimate points to a 176.4% upside. More than the range, one should note the standard deviation here, as it helps understand the variability of the estimates. The smaller the standard deviation, the greater the agreement among analysts.
While the consensus price target is a much-coveted metric for investors, solely banking on this metric to make an investment decision may not be wise at all. That's because the ability and unbiasedness of analysts in setting price targets have long been questionable.
However, an impressive consensus price target is not the only factor that indicates a potential upside in INTU. This view is strengthened by the agreement among analysts that the company will report better earnings than what they estimated earlier. Though a positive trend in earnings estimate revisions doesn't give any idea as to how much the stock could surge, it has proven effective in predicting an upside.
Zacks Price, Consensus and EPS Surprise Chart for INTU
Here's What You May Not Know About Analysts' Price Targets
According to researchers at several universities across the globe, a price target is one of many pieces of information about a stock that misleads investors far more often than it guides. In fact, empirical research shows that price targets set by several analysts, irrespective of the extent of agreement, rarely indicate where the price of a stock could actually be heading.
While Wall Street analysts have deep knowledge of a company's fundamentals and the sensitivity of its business to economic and industry issues, many of them tend to set overly optimistic price targets. Are you wondering why?
They usually do that to drum up interest in shares of companies that their firms either have existing business relationships with or are looking to be associated with. In other words, business incentives of firms covering a stock often result in inflated price targets set by analysts.
However, a tight clustering of price targets, which is represented by a low standard deviation, indicates that analysts have a high degree of agreement about the direction and magnitude of a stock's price movement. While that doesn't necessarily mean the stock will hit the average price target, it could be a good starting point for further research aimed at identifying the potential fundamental driving forces.
That said, while investors should not entirely ignore price targets, making an investment decision solely based on them could lead to disappointing ROI. So, price targets should always be treated with a high degree of skepticism.
There has been increasing optimism among analysts lately about the company's earnings prospects, as indicated by strong agreement among them in revising EPS estimates higher. And that could be a legitimate reason to expect an upside in the stock. After all, empirical research shows a strong correlation between trends in earnings estimate revisions and near-term stock price movements.
Over the last 30 days, the Zacks Consensus Estimate for the current year has increased 0%, as one estimate has moved higher compared to no negative revision.
Moreover, INTU currently has a Zacks Rank #2 (Buy), which means it is in the top 20% of more than 4,000 stocks that we rank based on four factors related to earnings estimates. Given an impressive externally-audited track record, this is a more conclusive indication of the stock's potential upside in the near term. You can see the complete list of today's Zacks Rank #1 (Strong Buy) stocks here >>>> .
Therefore, while the consensus price target may not be a reliable indicator of how much INTU could gain, the direction of price movement it implies does appear to be a good guide.

Intuit has rolled out its Intuit Intelligence platform globally across QuickBooks and Intuit Accountant Suite, bringing AI driven automation, reporting and workflow tools to millions of small businesses and accounting firms, with features now in beta for international QuickBooks Online and QuickBooks Online Advanced customers.
Early user data from Intuit Intelligence points to meaningful productivity shifts, with reported monthly time savings for customers and more accountant hours redirected toward advisory work, which directly links the AI platform to how efficiently Intuit's products can be used in real firms.

To remain a shareholder in Intuit, you need to believe its AI-led system of intelligence across tax, small business, and mid-market products continues to deepen usage and support margin progress. The key short-term swing factor is whether Intuit Intelligence drives better customer engagement following recent softness in new customer additions and DIY tax share.
The biggest near-term risk is that lower-priced entry offers and Mailchimp simplification do not rebuild customer growth, leaving revenue and earnings below expectations. The international rollout of Intuit Intelligence appears additive to the core thesis, but it does not fundamentally change the fact that execution risk around customer acquisition remains central.
The extension of Intuit Intelligence across international QuickBooks and Intuit Accountant Suite ties directly into the existing AI catalyst that analysts have focused on. More workflows touched by automation can reinforce the value of QuickBooks, money and workforce solutions, and the Enterprise Suite for both small firms and mid-market clients.
The same announcement also highlights risk. With 10 million customers feeding the platform and complex AI workflows embedded in compliance-heavy products, any missteps in accuracy, transparency, or legal scrutiny around AI or marketing claims could affect costs and confidence. For you as an investor, execution quality on this global rollout is now a key factor to watch.
What The Current Intuit Forecasts Assume
Analysts are effectively asking you to underwrite a very specific path for Intuit as AI becomes more deeply woven into its tax and accounting workflows. The consensus view assumes revenue grows at 8.9% a year over the next few years and that profit margins step up from 21.3% today to 24.8% by year three. That margin lift, combined with steady share count reduction of about 4.01% a year, underpins forecasts that earnings move from US$4.6b today to US$6.9b by 2029, while the stock trades on a P/E of 18x those projected profits compared with 16.1x on current earnings.
On these numbers, the implied valuation for Intuit also rests on where you think it should sit relative to the wider US software group. The consensus view uses a future P/E that is below the reported 29.7x for the industry, even as analysts model higher margins and revenue expansion tied to Intuit Intelligence and the company's broader product ecosystem. That disconnect matters because it indicates expectations for operating performance are reasonably ambitious, but the implied P/E multiple is not at the very top of sector ranges based on the data provided.
Price targets bring these assumptions together into a single reference point for the stock. The average analyst target sits at US$405.60, which is 32% above the quoted share price of US$275.71, with a wide range from US$290 on the low end to US$732 at the high end. For you as a shareholder or prospective investor, the key test is whether the AI led growth story and the shift in customer acquisition tactics make the path to US$27.7b of revenue and US$6.9b of earnings by 2029 feel realistic enough for that target to be a useful benchmark.
Intuit's current consensus outlook points to revenues of US$27.7b and earnings of US$6.9b by 2029, built on 8.9% yearly revenue growth and an earnings increase of about US$2.3b from US$4.6b today.

Intuit to Acquire Sequence to Boost AI-Powered Mid-Market Offerings
Mon, October 19, 2026 at 7:20 AM CDT 2 min read
Intuit Inc. INTU has announced an agreement to acquire Sequence, an AI-native revenue management platform, to expand its capabilities in the mid-market enterprise resource planning (ERP) space. The acquisition is expected to strengthen Intuit Enterprise Suite and QuickBooks Online Advanced by integrating automated quote-to-revenue workflows, including pricing, billing, collections and revenue recognition. The move aligns with Intuit's strategy to attract growing businesses seeking alternatives to traditional ERP solutions offered by Oracle ORCL and SAP SAP.
Sequence's platform replaces manual billing processes and spreadsheets with AI-powered automation, supporting complex revenue models based on consumption, usage, seats and milestones. These capabilities could help Intuit expand into industries such as B2B software and professional services, where hybrid pricing structures are becoming increasingly common. By simplifying revenue management and reducing administrative workloads, Intuit could improve customer retention and attract businesses that might otherwise consider more established enterprise solutions from Oracle and SAP.
The acquisition also strengthens Intuit's positioning in an increasingly competitive market for AI-enabled financial software. Oracle offers integrated subscription and revenue management capabilities through its cloud applications, while SAP provides subscription billing and revenue recognition solutions within its enterprise software ecosystem.
Intuit's strategy of combining AI-native automation with its existing financial management platform could help differentiate its offerings among mid-market customers seeking simpler and more integrated solutions. Sequence's AI engineering expertise could accelerate product innovation and support Intuit's ambition to develop a comprehensive AI-native ERP platform.
The acquisition could create cross-selling opportunities across Intuit's existing customer base while expanding its addressable market in more complex business segments. While competition from Oracle and SAP remains significant, the addition of Sequence could reinforce Intuit's long-term growth prospects by broadening its mid-market capabilities and strengthening its AI-driven financial software ecosystem.

The word INTUIT is displayed in blue capital letters on a white smartphone screen, against a blurred pink and purple background. (Credit: Photo: PJ McDonnell/Shutterstock)
Sun, October 18, 2026 at 4:30 PM CDT 6 min read
Benzinga and Yahoo Finance LLC may earn commission or revenue on some items through the links below.
Intuit Inc. stock is trading higher by more than 6% on Thursday after the company announced to acquire Sequence, an AI-native revenue management platform.
The acquisition expands Intuit's revenue management offerings for mid-market businesses.
Founded in 2021, Sequence leverages AI to help B2B finance and commercial teams automate the full quote-to-revenue lifecycle, including deal configuration and pricing, billing, invoicing, collections, and revenue recognition.

The acquisition will strengthen the capabilities of Intuit's Intuit Enterprise Suite, a resource planning and consolidation platform, and QuickBooks Online Advanced, its cloud-based accounting platform.
The acquisition will also expand Intuit's reach to sectors, including B2B software, professional services, construction, healthcare, and manufacturing.
Sequence co-founder and CEO Riya Grover highlighted the growing need for revenue management automation as business complexity grows with usage-based and hybrid pricing revenue models.
Ashley Still, executive vice president and general manager, Small Business & Mid-Market Group at Intuit, said the acquisition further extends Intuit Enterprise Suite directly into industries that increasingly leverage AI consumption models and is a meaningful step forward for the company to deliver AI-native ERP for complex businesses.
Following the acquisition, Grover and the Sequence team will join Intuit's Mid-Market product organization.
Intuit held $4.7 billion in cash and cash equivalents and had total debt of $7.7 billion as of July 31.
Financial terms of the deal were not disclosed.

GAAP EPS is projected at $20.12 to $20.36, while adjusted EPS is expected at $22.88 to $23.12, compared with the analyst consensus estimate of $24.04.
The company expects first-quarter fiscal 2027 revenues between $4.29 billion to $4.31 billion and adjusted EPS at $2.44 to $2.48.

Building Wealth Across More Than Just the Market
Building a resilient portfolio means thinking beyond a single asset or market trend. Economic cycles shift, sectors rise and fall, and no one investment performs well in every environment. That's why many investors look to diversify with platforms that provide access to real estate, fixed-income opportunities, precious metals, and even self-directed retirement accounts. By spreading exposure across multiple asset classes, it becomes easier to manage risk, capture steady returns, and create long-term wealth that isn't tied to the fortunes of just one company or industry.
For accredited investors looking beyond stocks and bonds, EquityMultiple provides access to vetted commercial real estate deals starting at $5,000, with only ~5% of opportunities passing their due diligence process.
Backed by Jeff Bezos, Arrived Homes makes real estate investing accessible with a low barrier to entry. Investors can buy fractional shares of single-family rentals and vacation homes starting with as little as $100. This allows everyday investors to diversify into real estate, collect rental income, and build long-term wealth without needing to manage properties directly.
Entertainment franchises can become valuable long-term assets when they successfully expand across multiple platforms. Skybound Entertainment, the company behind The Walking Dead and Invincible, develops original intellectual property that spans comics, television, film, video games, merchandise, and licensing. With more than 250 IPs in its portfolio and a strategy focused on retaining franchise rights while scaling successful stories across media, Skybound offers investors exposure to the growing entertainment and creator economy through a private company rather than traditional public market investments.
As artificial intelligence drives a surge in electricity demand, reliable power generation is becoming a critical part of the technology ecosystem. American PowerGen is developing natural gas-fired power plants in Texas, a fast-growing market fueled by AI data centers, manufacturing expansion, and population growth. By advancing projects through permitting, fuel supply, and grid interconnection, the company is positioning itself to help meet rising energy needs while offering investors exposure to the infrastructure supporting the next wave of AI and industrial growth.
As AI coding tools take on more of the work traditionally done by developers, companies are facing new challenges around code quality, context and the rising cost of AI-powered development. Bito is building software designed to help AI coding agents better understand complex codebases while helping companies control AI development costs. Founded by former PubMatic executives, Bito has raised more than $10 million from institutional and individual investors and is now raising additional capital through a Wefunder offering, giving investors an opportunity to invest in a company targeting an emerging need within the rapidly expanding AI software market.
For accredited investors looking beyond stocks and traditional real estate opportunities, DLP Capital provides access to private real estate strategies focused on workforce housing — homes for essential workers such as teachers, nurses, firefighters, and police officers. With more than $5.5 billion in assets under management and a community of 4,000+ accredited investors, DLP Capital gives investors access to real estate strategies designed around the growing need for housing that working Americans can actually afford.
Farmland has historically held its value through market volatility and delivered returns uncorrelated to stocks and bonds. For accredited investors, FarmTogether offers direct access to high-quality U.S. farmland starting at $15,000 — fully managed, with no landlord headaches.
Private real estate and private credit can add income and stability to a stock-heavy portfolio. Fundrise offers access to diversified private real estate and credit strategies through an easy-to-use platform, with professionally managed portfolios designed to generate passive income and long-term growth.

SAXONBURG, Pa., Sept. 21, 2026 (GLOBE NEWSWIRE) -- Coherent Corp. (NYSE: COHR), the global leader in photonics, today announced PhotonLink™, an integrated optics platform that brings together Coherent’s broad portfolio of critical photonics technologies, precision assembly and test capabilities to deliver complete optical solutions for next-generation AI datacenters. The platform supports co-packaged optics (CPO), near-packaged optics (NPO) and emerging chip to chip connectivity.
As AI systems continue to scale, demand for higher bandwidth and lower power is driving optical connectivity closer to compute and switching silicon. These architectures require lasers, silicon photonics, precision optics, fibers and detectors to work together. PhotonLink brings those technologies and the expertise to integrate them into one platform.
“The next leap in AI requires more than faster chips – it requires a new way to connect them,” said Jim Anderson, Chief Executive Officer at Coherent. “Customers need complete optical solutions, not just individual components. Coherent is uniquely positioned to bring together the critical technologies, integrate and test the finished assemblies, and manufacture them at scale. PhotonLink puts that capability to work for the next generation of AI infrastructure.”
Coherent’s vertical integration spans compound semiconductor materials, lasers, optics and specialty fiber through final assembly and test. PhotonLink gives customers access to both individual components and complete optical assemblies from one partner, helping simplify system design, streamline qualification and reduce the complexity of integrating technologies from multiple suppliers.
FROM CRITICAL TECHNOLOGIES TO COMPLETE OPTICAL ASSEMBLIES
The PhotonLink platform spans four functions of the optical path: Generate, Shape, Guide and Receive. The portfolio includes indium phosphide (InP) lasers, vertical-cavity surface-emitting laser (VCSEL) arrays, silicon photonics, isolators, specialty fibers, micro-optics and detectors. Coherent integrates these technologies into external laser sources, precision fiber assemblies and optical modules tailored to customer architectures.
CUSTOMER ENGAGEMENT AND MANUFACTURING SCALE
Coherent has more than ten CPO customer engagements and more than ten NPO engagements, with anchor customers and long-term agreements secured for both architectures. The company also has more than five engagements in emerging chip to chip connectivity. Revenue from the PhotonLink platform is expected to begin ramping in Q4 of CY2026.
PhotonLink builds on Coherent’s established datacenter manufacturing base, which has shipped more than 300 million InP lasers and more than one billion InP and gallium arsenide (GaAs) photodetectors. Coherent is expanding its 6” InP and specialty fiber manufacturing capacity to support the PhotonLink ramp.
Coherent hosted a PhotonLink launch event on September 21 at the Gran Hotel Miramar in Málaga during the European Conference on Optical Communication (ECOC) 2026. The presentation and webcast recording are available at PHOTONLINK™ Launch webcast
Visitors to ECOC 2026 can also meet Coherent experts and explore PhotonLink at Stand 2100, Hall 2, at FYCMA - Trade Fair & Congress Center in Málaga, Spain.
For more information about PhotonLink, visit https://www.coherent.com/datacenter-communications/photonlink
Coherent is the global photonics leader. We harness photons to drive innovation. Industry leaders in the datacenter, communications, and industrial markets rely on Coherent’s world-leading technology to fuel their own innovation and growth. Founded in 1971 and operating in more than 20 countries, Coherent brings the industry’s broadest, deepest technology stack; unmatched supply chain resilience; and global scale to help its customers solve their toughest technology challenges. For more information, visit coherent.com.

Is Coherent (COHR) Fairly Valued?
Mon, October 19, 2026 at 9:15 PM CDT 4 min read
Coherent (NYSE:COHR) reports its fiscal first-quarter results early next month, and it has already set a high bar. Management told investors to expect revenue between $2.2 billion and $2.4 billion, up from the $2.05 billion it reported last quarter.
But the stock is priced as if that growth might not last. It trades at about 24.7 times estimated fiscal 2027 earnings, which is below its own five-year average. Consensus still calls for strong adjusted earnings growth that year. A faster-growing business at a lower multiple than its history raises the question of whether investors are being too cautious.
Coherent makes the lasers, optical parts, and networking components that move data inside AI data centers and across telecom networks. Its Datacenter & Communications segment, by far its largest, brought in $1.615 billion last quarter, up from $1.018 billion a year earlier. The results lean toward a stock that is cheaper than they justify, with one big condition: its customers have to keep spending.
Data Center Sales Are Driving the Growth
Growth has sped up sharply. Over the past five years, Coherent's revenue grew about 18% a year, and last quarter it rose 34% from a year earlier, well above that pace. On a pro forma basis, which adjusts for businesses Coherent has sold, the quarter's growth was 42%.
The product mix is moving the same way. Last month, Coherent launched PhotonLink, a platform that bundles its lasers, detectors, and other optical parts for AI data centers. Yahoo Finance reported that the company counts 20 customer engagements so far, and that Nvidia invested about $4 billion in Coherent and Lumentum earlier this year. For investors looking to add exposure to AI data center optics, our list of 10 Best Fiber Optics Stocks to Buy for the AI Data Center Boom is worth a look.
Nvidia Backed a $50 Billion AI Data-Center IPO. Wall Street Just Hit the Brakes
Adjusted operating margin reached 21.8% last quarter, up from 18.0% a year earlier, so each dollar of new sales kept more profit. Adjusted earnings per share rose $0.74 from a year earlier, to $1.74. Investors who want more high-growth stocks can see our ranking of 10 Best Aggressive Growth Stocks to Buy According to Wall Street Analysts.
The adjusted figure runs well above the GAAP one: GAAP earnings per share were $1.19 last quarter, against $1.74 on the adjusted basis. Earnings estimates, and the multiple built on them, use the adjusted number, so the gap matters to anyone paying for the stock.
Most of the growth comes from AI data centers, so a pause in spending by the companies building them would reach Coherent quickly. Management described customer demand in its latest release as exceptional, and its guidance for the coming quarter sits above what it just reported. One reading of the lower multiple is that buyers want a discount for that dependence. The next report will show whether demand is still arriving at that level.
What Investors Are Paying for That Growth
At about 24.7 times estimated earnings for the fiscal year ending next June, Coherent trades above the 21.01 median for its sector. It sits below its own five-year average of 27.46. Against expected adjusted earnings growth of about 68% for the same year, the premium to its sector looks small. If you're looking for cheaper AI names, check out 10 Undervalued AI Stocks to Buy Now.
The price assumes that growth will slow or that customer spending will stall before those earnings arrive. If you own the stock, you own it at a lower price against earnings than it has usually carried, in exchange for taking on that spending risk.
Are investors being too cautious? Faster sales, wider margins, and a multiple below the stock's own history suggest they are pricing in more doubt than the numbers show. Next month's report is the thing to watch: whether revenue lands in the guided range, and whether the data center business keeps growing at last quarter's pace.

Traders positioned ahead of the November 5 report, watching for updates on AI-related optical demand and capacity utilization.

Coherent Benefits From AI Networking Focus
Coherent stock rose more modestly. The company has launched its PhotonLink integrated optics platform designed for co-packaged optics, near-packaged optics, and chip-to-chip connectivity. Coherent already has more than 10 customer engagements in these areas, with initial PhotonLink revenue expected to ramp in the December quarter.

The broader chip sector has also shown signs of stabilizing after a recent soft stretch.
Upcoming earnings will provide the next major checkpoints for order visibility and margin trends across the three companies. Lumentum’s multiyear capacity constraints and Coherent’s PhotonLink ramp offer potential catalysts if demand remains robust. Applied Optoelectronics faces similar questions around AI optical adoption and competitive positioning.
Investors should consider keeping their position sizes modest given the volatility typical of optics and photonics stocks. Global optical fiber demand is projected to reach 577 million fiber-kilometers in 2026, with data centers accounting for a growing share.

TrendForce forecasts a global optical fiber supply shortfall of 180 million fiber-kilometers in 2026.
Spot prices for bend-insensitive fiber used inside data centers are projected to average more than five times their 2025 levels.
Expanding optical fiber preform capacity typically takes 18 to 24 months, limiting how quickly manufacturers can respond.

Shares of Corning Inc. (GLW) and Verizon Communications Inc. (VZ) are in focus after research firm TrendForce forecast on Monday that rising artificial intelligence (AI) infrastructure demand would leave the global optical fiber market facing a supply shortfall of 180 million fiber-kilometers in 2026.
The firm expects shortages to persist until at least 2028. Separately, it projects spot prices for finished optical fiber products to reach 2.8 to more than five times their 2025 levels in 2026, depending on the fiber type.

Other fiber-related stocks also came into focus, including Coherent (COHR), Ciena (CIEN), and Amphenol (APH), given their exposure to fiber-optic connectivity, optical components and high-capacity networking infrastructure.
Advertisement|Remove ads.
According to TrendForce, global optical fiber demand is expected to reach 577 million fiber-kilometers this year, with data centers accounting for roughly 18% to 20% of consumption. That share is projected to climb to 30% to 35% in 2027.
TrendForce said AI data-center demand has tightened global supply since late 2025, with chipmakers and telecom operators joining hyperscale cloud providers in investing in related infrastructure.
Unlike previous telecom infrastructure cycles, the firm said the current shortage reflects sustained additional demand from AI data centers, driving the need for interconnects and high-capacity backbone networks.
Advertisement|Remove ads.
Global optical fiber capacity utilization has climbed to 92%, while inventories have fallen from four months in 2024 to just one month. Some leading suppliers are already booked into the first quarter of 2027, while expanding preform capacity typically takes 18 to 24 months.
The pricing impact varies by application. Bend-insensitive fiber used inside data centers is projected to average more than five times its 2025 price, while AI backbone fiber prices are expected to reach approximately 2.8 times their 2025 levels. Mainstream telecom fiber quotations could rise to around 3.7 times their previous levels.
Corning, Verizon Lock In Long-Term Fiber Supply
TrendForce said telecom operators are already shifting from short-term purchases to long-term supply agreements to secure future fiber requirements.
Advertisement|Remove ads.
The firm highlighted a September agreement between Corning and Verizon covering approximately 129 million fiber kilometers, or 80 million fiber miles, of high-density optical fiber and connectivity solutions.
Corning also signed a separate agreement worth more than $3 billion with AT&T (T) in September to supply fiber and cable for its U.S. network expansion.
TrendForce expects such agreements to become increasingly common as AI-related demand continues to grow and manufacturers face lengthy capacity expansion timelines.

Coherent (COHR) Could Benefit From AI Networking Even if CPO Adoption Takes Time
Mon, October 19, 2026 at 8:47 AM CDT 3 min read
Coherent Corp. (NYSE:COHR) is preparing for the next phase of AI data center expansion. On September 21, the company launched PhotonLink, an integrated optics platform. It is designed for co-packaged optics, near-packaged optics, and chip-to-chip connectivity. The company already has more than 10 customer engagements for both CPO and near-packaged optics, with initial PhotonLink revenue expected to ramp in the December quarter. In my view, Coherent's advantage lies in its ability to bring several essential optical technologies together in one solution. This could make it a more valuable supplier to customers. The company's integrated optics strategy could give it a larger role in the AI buildout. Curious which other stocks are riding a similar CPO growth trend? Coherent Could Benefit From AI Networking Even if CPO Adoption Takes Time
Why I Think Coherent Has More Room to Grow
What makes me bullish on Coherent is that it does not have to wait for CPO to become mainstream to benefit from AI networking demand. Its existing optical business is already growing rapidly, while PhotonLink gives it another opportunity to capture growth. This shows that even if adoption is slower than expected, the company can still benefit from demand for its existing optical products.
Moreover, a TD Cowen analyst made a point two months ago that supports my view. Sean O'Loughlin reiterated a Buy rating on COHR with a $395 price target on Aug 13. He pointed to opportunities in high-speed optical transceivers and newer technologies such as CPO for the company. I think this supports the case that Coherent has multiple ways to benefit from the expansion of AI infrastructure.
Coherent's growth opportunities come with a valuation risk. Its forward non-GAAP P/E of 30.57x is about 12% above its five-year average of 27.42x and well above the sector median of 22.87x. Its forward price-to-sales ratio of 5.34x is even more stretched, sitting about 90% above its five-year average of 2.81x. I believe these multiples suggest investors are already pricing in strong growth from AI networking. PhotonLink could help justify the premium if adoption gains momentum. But if AI networking demand slows or PhotonLink takes longer to gain traction, the stock could come under pressure. In my view, this is a risk that cannot be ignored, but for an emerging technology that could change the landscape of many data centers, investors have the option to either wait for more visibility into future earnings or take on the risk. Fewer hedge funds held Coherent in Q2, with the count falling from 114 in Q1 to 105 in Q2. However, in Q1, hedge funds had invested around $3.9 billion in the stock, a figure that grew to $4.62 billion by Q2.

Coherent (NYSE:COHR | COHR Price Prediction) is priced at $263.23, while the average analyst price target sits at $412.52. The difference points to about 56.7% upside.
Coherent makes lasers, optical transceivers and photonic components. Its Datacenter & Communications division now brings in 79% of revenue. With funding from NVIDIA (NASDAQ:NVDA), which invested $2B, Coherent also joined the S&P 500 during fiscal 2026.
The gap matters because the business keeps speeding up while the stock goes the other way. With implied upside above 40%, Wall Street is saying the market has mispriced one of the main suppliers of AI connectivity.
Record Quarters and Falling Shares Open a Six-Month Disconnect
Most of the decline came in a single week. Coherent fell 21.32% over the past week, including a 9.22% drop in the latest session. That session came right after a hot inflation report drove the 30-year Treasury yield as high as 5.63%. AI infrastructure names fell, a cloud provider falling 16% and a server maker 11%. Rising rates hit capital-hungry suppliers hardest. Coherent spent $1.103B on capex in fiscal 2026 but generated only $79.5M in operating cash flow.
Over six months, shares are down 15.98%, and the stock trades about 40% below its 52-week high of $440. Optics stocks fell on profit taking with no company news behind it. Earlier, a fiber maker’s $2B at-the-market equity offering dragged Coherent 11% lower in sympathy.
Coherent’s own results stayed strong. Coherent has beaten EPS estimates 4 consecutive times. Its latest quarter delivered non-GAAP EPS of $1.74 versus $1.6171 expected, on revenue up 33.7%.
Rosenblatt’s $500 Target Calls for Shares to Nearly Double
Mike Genovese at Rosenblatt Securities holds the highest target on Wall Street at $500.00 with a Buy rating. That target means 89.9% upside. His thesis rests on three things: an AI transceiver super-cycle, production that is sold out well in advance, and margins that expand as manufacturing scale catches up with demand.
Management’s own comments support that view. “Fiscal 27 is basically completely booked out,” the CEO said. Customer orders reach into calendar 28, and long-term agreements run through the end of the decade. Coherent expects its first quarter above $3 billion in revenue by the end of fiscal 2027. Current-quarter guidance calls for revenue of $2.20B to $2.40B and EPS of $1.85 to $2.05.
Analysts are watching specific catalysts. Indium phosphide output is set to double this quarter, one quarter ahead of plan. Co-packaged optics revenue begins ramping in fiscal Q2. Optical circuit switching targets more than $4 billion of addressable market. Management also keeps its gross margin target above 42%.
Of 24 analysts, 4 have it at Strong Buy, 15 at Buy and 5 at Hold, with zero Sells. Bernstein recently started coverage at Outperform (247 Wall St.). Still, targets are estimates and carry no guarantee. The trailing P/E of 68x against a forward P/E of 30x shows how much of the thesis depends on earnings that have yet to arrive.
Fabrinet Carries the Optics Group’s Deepest Discount
The whole peer group sold off together. Coherent’s decline is a sector event.
Lumentum (NASDAQ:LITE) fell 19.33% over the past week but remains up 143.18% year to date. At $896.33 against a $1177.34 target, implied upside is 31.4%, which is smaller than Coherent’s. Coverage is heavily bullish, with 5 Strong Buys, 18 Buys and 4 Holds.
Fabrinet (NYSE:FN) dropped 21.09% for the week and is down 13.69% year to date. At $392.93 against a $734.11 target, it shows 86.8% implied upside. Coverage is lighter, with 3 Strong Buys, 4 Buys and 2 Holds among 9 analysts.
Fabrinet carries the largest consensus upside in the group. Coherent sits in the middle, offering a bigger discount than Lumentum with wider coverage than Fabrinet.
Coherent Still Beats the S&P 500 Despite the Slide
At $263.23, Coherent trades well below the $412.52 consensus target, leaving 56.7% implied upside across 24 covering analysts.
The six-month decline of 15.98% hides a strong year. Shares are up 42.62% year to date, while the S&P 500 has gained 12.86%. Over one year, Coherent is up 140.68%.
Coherent’s Booked Backlog Outweighs the Rate Risk
The bullish case improves if Coherent keeps converting its sold-out backlog into revenue on schedule and gross margin keeps climbing toward 42%. The outlook weakens if long-term rates keep rising, the heavy capex keeps burning cash, or hyperscaler spending cools off before co-packaged optics and optical circuit switching reach scale.
A $3 billion quarter and margin expansion would make the consensus target look conservative. On the risk side, Coherent carries about $3.2B of long-term debt and a beta of 2.113, so every move in rates gets amplified.
Contracted demand into calendar 2028 suggests this selloff reflects a rate and sentiment reset. The stock’s high beta points to continued volatility.

Coherent Corp. has recently reported strong AI-driven demand for its optical connectivity portfolio, expanded and sold-out capacity for key data center components into 2029, and ambitious plans to double manufacturing output and indium phosphide capacity over the next year to meet infrastructure needs.
An interesting twist is CIBC's decision to list a Coherent Canadian Depositary Receipt on the TSX, broadening access for Canadian investors just as the company leans heavily into AI data center buildouts and advanced optical networking technologies.

The near term catalyst is whether sold out capacity into 2029 and the upcoming November earnings update reinforce confidence in that AI backlog. The biggest risk is that heavy capital spending for capacity and PhotonLink ramps fails to translate into sustained cash generation. Recent share volatility after macro and sector selloffs does not materially change that core trade off.
Among recent updates, the PhotonLink integrated optics platform launch stands out. It directly ties into Coherent's AI data center catalyst by targeting 1.6T-class transceivers, co packaged and near packaged optics, and chip to chip links that hyperscalers are testing right now. If customer adoption tracks current interest, PhotonLink could help fill the expanded indium phosphide and module capacity that is already committed into 2029, potentially supporting better utilization and margins if demand holds up.

Warnings from two chip giants about AI funding constraints have sent optical networking stocks into a sharp sector-wide slide, and the smallest supplier in the group faces the steepest drop despite record revenue and a CEO forecasting demand that outpaces…
Published October 14, 2026, 12:35pm ET · 3 min read
Market Movers desk. Editor: David Moadel.
The rapid flow of data through fiber optics symbolizes the strong performance and potential for Applied Optoelectronics (AAOI) as its stock continues to climb. © Fiber optics lights abstract background (Shutterstock.com) by asharkyu
Optical networking suppliers are sliding again, and Applied Optoelectronics (NASDAQ:AAOI) stock is falling the most as doubts about how artificial intelligence (AI) infrastructure gets funded spread through the group. Applied Optoelectronics stock is at $88.99, down 9% in afternoon trading, though it remains up 155% year to date.
Meanwhile, Coherent Corp. (NYSE:COHR | COHR Price Prediction) stock is at $269.33, down 7% as it follows its smaller peer lower. Likewise, Lumentum Holdings (NASDAQ:LITE) stock is at $920.42, down 7% in step with Coherent. Such a tight range of losses points to a sector-wide revaluation of AI connectivity suppliers.
Thematic funds are feeling the pressure as well, and the Roundhill Photonics & Optics ETF (CBOE:LYTE) is down 8%. Lumentum and Coherent were the fund’s two largest holdings as of August 6, while Applied Optoelectronics carried a far smaller weight in the basket. The SPDR S&P 500 ETF Trust (NYSEARCA:SPY) is down 1%, a softer decline that shows how tightly the selling is concentrated in optical names.
Broadcom and Intel Funding Warnings Rattle Optical Names
Optical networking shares began selling off on October 12. The slide came after Broadcom (NASDAQ:AVGO) chief executive Hock Tan stated access to capital could become a bigger constraint on AI expansion than chip shortages. Intel (NASDAQ:INTC) chief executive Lip-Bu Tan also pointed to rising borrowing costs and uncertainty over returns on AI investments. Along with other optical names, Lumentum stock finished among the market’s biggest losers that day.
The selling has continued since, and no company-specific development explains this session’s move in Applied Optoelectronics stock. Applied Optoelectronics completed an at-the-market equity program, raising capital to fund the capacity expansion its optical component business needs. Its completion announcement came on October 5, days before the funding warnings from Broadcom and Intel.
Smallest Supplier Faces the Biggest Capacity Test
Lasers, transceivers and optical components from Applied Optoelectronics, Coherent and Lumentum move data between servers inside AI data centers. Their revenue tracks hyperscale spending. So the group is sensitive to any sign that budgets could tighten (we covered seven non-chipmaker suppliers riding the same AI expansion in a free report here). By far the smallest of the group, Applied Optoelectronics also sells into cable broadband networks, which gives it a revenue base Coherent and Lumentum don’t share.
Record results support the bull case. In Q2 2026, Applied Optoelectronics posted revenue of $191.92 million, up 86.4% year over year, as its datacenter segment more than doubled. The company also returned to adjusted profitability, earning $0.06 per share against a $0.015 estimate.
On the company’s August 6 call, chief executive Thompson Lin stated, “Demand to support next-generation AI infrastructure remains so robust that our near-term revenue is bounded almost entirely by production capacity and key component availability.” Management then guided Q3 2026 revenue to $255 million to $290 million. Lin also forecast that demand would outpace production capacity through mid-2027.
Hyperscale Orders Decide the Expansion Payoff
The open question for Applied Optoelectronics is whether hyperscale customers keep placing orders at the pace its expanded capacity assumes. Its top 10 customers accounted for 99% of Q2 2026 revenue, which leaves little buffer if one large buyer slows down its spending or delays deliveries. Applied Optoelectronics still posted a net loss under generally accepted accounting principles in that quarter, a reminder that its rapid expansion is costly.
Coherent and Lumentum struck a confident tone in August. On an August 12 call, Coherent chief executive Jim Anderson stated, “We continue to see no signs of attenuation in customer demand.” Lumentum chief executive Michael Hurlston added that “data center architects are turning to optical links as a primary means of connectivity,” and the company guided Q1 FY2027 revenue to $1.225 billion to $1.275 billion.
Those remarks came weeks before the funding warnings from Broadcom and Intel, so fresh order commentary from these suppliers could show whether this pullback reflects a real shift in demand. Bernstein initiated Cisco Systems (NASDAQ:CSCO) and Corning with Market Perform ratings, providing a more balanced view of an industry that has rallied sharply on AI-related expectations.

Lumentum could benefit from demand for high-speed networking, optical switching, transceivers, and other hardware needed to connect AI computing systems. Yet Lumentum faces execution risk as the company expands output, with management previously acknowledging that shipments of high-powered lasers were behind demand.

Coherent stock, Lumentum stock, and Corning stock all moved higher as traders returned to a group that benefits from expectations for rising AI network traffic and increasingly demanding data-center architectures.
The Coherent stock rally could continue if AI-related orders, customer commentary, and capital-spending plans remain supportive. However, the same theme creates risk if large customers delay infrastructure spending, if competitors build excess capacity, or if elevated expectations leave less room for execution mistakes.
Coherent has a compelling product catalyst in PhotonLink and a new Outperform rating to support the bullish discussion. CRDO vs. COHR: Which AI Connectivity Stock Is the Better Buy?
Thu, October 15, 2026 at 9:14 AM CDT 7 min read
Both Credo Technology Group Holding Ltd CRDO and Coherent Corp COHR are beneficiaries of the AI data center buildout, but approach the opportunity from different angles.
Credo specializes in high-speed connectivity solutions, including integrated circuits (ICs), retimers, optical DSPs, Active Electrical Cables (AECs), SerDes chiplets and SerDes IP licensing.
Coherent is a manufacturer of lasers, transceivers, optoelectronic devices and modules, and engineered materials for verticals spanning industrial, instrumentation, communications and electronics markets.
For investors, the choice between CRDO and COHR is not straightforward. Let us break down the fundamentals, valuations, growth outlook and risks for each company to determine which stock stands out.
As AI clusters grow larger, connectivity is emerging as a critical constraint. Management highlighted that the challenge is no longer just bandwidth, but also reliability, power efficiency, signal integrity, telemetry and serviceability. Credo believes its system-level approach, which combines silicon, firmware, manufacturing tests and qualification, remains a key differentiator.
AEC is a system-level product for CRDO and its core growth engine. The company now has deep relationships with five hyperscalers, alongside expanding engagement with Neocloud customers. Credo continues to see higher AEC penetration within existing customers as deployments scale, while the shift toward 200-gig-per-lane 1.6T ports provides another growth opportunity.
The retimer business is another lucrative opportunity. Management noted that the retimer business also delivered record quarterly revenues, supported by scale-up deployments of Screaming Eagle at 100-gig-per-lane and initial contributions from its 200-gig-per-lane Blue Heron retimer.
The most significant shift in Credo's business mix is unfolding in its optical segment. On the last earnings call, management added that it continues to project more than $600 million in optical revenues, with ZeroFlap optics, silicon photonics PICs and optical DSPs each contributing over $100 million. Credo added that its optical DSP business generated "record revenues" in the fiscal first quarter. The company also recognized its first silicon-photonics PIC revenues following the DustPhotonics acquisition, with initial wins involving 800-gig and 1.6T optical transceivers. Credo continues to forecast more than 85% year-over-year revenue growth for fiscal 2027, aided by an expected second-half inflection.
The company's recent product announcements further strengthen its growth prospects. At the October 2026 OCP Global Summit, the company introduced its 1.6T ZeroFlap Active Light Cable ("ALC"). The wide-parallel optical interconnect solution is built for next-generation AI infrastructure, addressing rising reliability and energy-efficiency requirements. The solution targets AI scale-out and front-end networks, strengthening Credo's position in next-generation optical interconnects. Shipments are expected to begin in 2027.
Alongside the new ALC, the company announced the launch of the Short-Reach Micro-Emitter Optics Workstream within the Open Compute Project community. The initiative, backed by a leading hyperscaler and optical technology providers, including AFL, ams OSRAM and BizLink, aims to advance the development of the wide, parallel optical connectivity ecosystem.
The latest developments build on the company's expanding product portfolio. In September 2026, Credo launched its new family of 224G-based ZF optical transceivers. The new products extend Credo's ZF architecture to 1.6T port speeds and combine its 224G-per-lane optical DSP with the Kfir200 silicon photonics-based PICs and latest-generation PILOT diagnostics platform. The products are available in 2xDR4, 2xFR4 and DR8 configurations, supporting a range of AI scale-out interconnect architectures.
CRDO's growth does not come without meaningful risks. In the fiscal first quarter, four customers generated roughly 84% of quarterly revenues. Customer concentration is a major concern as it exposes the company to shifts in customer spending decisions and could materially affect results.
Execution risk is another risk factor. Much of the expected growth in fiscal 2027 is dependent on a successful ramp in the optical business. Any delay in deployment or broader industry transitions could affect this ramp. Macroeconomic uncertainties and exposure to the AI investment cycle amid increasing market competition remain additional concerns. The DustPhotonics acquisition also reduced its cash balance to $764.3 million at the end of the fiscal first quarter.
Explosive growth in AI data center infrastructure is driving unprecedented demand for optical networking solutions, positioning Coherent for long-term growth.
The Datacenter & Communications segment remains Coherent's core engine, contributing 79% of total revenues in the fourth quarter of fiscal 2026. Segment revenues increased 59% year over year, while data center revenues surged 66% on broad-based strength. Growing adoption of 800G and 1.6T optical transceivers bodes well. Management expects the 1.6T transceiver ramp to accelerate in calendar 2026 and 2027 as customer adoption increases.
Coherent expects first-quarter fiscal 2027 revenues between $2.2 billion and $2.4 billion, with non-GAAP earnings per share of $1.85-$2.05. The company expects to achieve its first-ever quarter with over $3 billion in revenue by the end of fiscal 2027.
The launch of PhotonLink strengthens its product portfolio. This integrated optics platform combines lasers, silicon photonics, specialty fibers, isolators, specialty fibers, micro-optics and detectors to support co-packaged optics ("CPO"), near-packaged optics ("NPO") and emerging chip-to-chip connectivity. PhotonLink-related revenues are expected to begin ramping in the fourth quarter of calendar 2026.
Beyond transceivers, CPO, multi-rail systems, optical circuit switching ("OCS") and advanced materials for data center, thermal and power management offer additional growth opportunities. OCS revenues increased sequentially in the fiscal fourth quarter, while multi-rail revenues are expected to begin ramping in the first half of calendar 2027. The company expects OCS revenues to improve, supported by capacity expansion, in the upcoming quarters.
On the last earnings call, COHR noted that OCS represented more than $4 billion of addressable opportunity across data center interconnect, scale-up and scale-out networks. Further, management added that CPO, NPO and other forms of integrated optics represent more than $15 billion of incremental addressable opportunity over the coming years as these technologies enable the transition from copper connectivity.
Aggressive capacity expansion strategy bodes well. On the last earnings call, management said that the company was expanding its six-inch indium phosphide production capacity, targeting a doubling of internal output year over year by the end of the first quarter of fiscal 2027. Management expects capacity to more than double again by the end of calendar 2027.
However, the company is witnessing rising operating and capital expenses as it focuses on capacity expansion. While these investments are necessary for long-term growth, they may pressure margins and free cash flow if revenues do not materialize as expected. Capital expenditures reached $556 million in the fiscal fourth quarter, compared with $290 million in the preceding quarter, and management expects further sequential increase in the fiscal first quarter.
Heavy reliance on the Datacenter & Communications segment increases volatility linked to AI spending cycles amid increasing competition and macroeconomic troubles. Weakness in the Industrial segment, owing to softness in broader industrial markets, is concerning.
Price Performance & Valuations of CRDO & COHR
Year to date, CRDO and COHR are up 24.5% and 42.6%, respectively.
CRDO is trading at a forward price-to-earnings multiple of 23.41X, lower than COHR's 24.73X.
How Do the Consensus Estimates Compare for CRDO & COHR?
Analysts have raised their earnings estimates for COHR by 0.9% for the current fiscal year in the past 60 days.
Estimates have been revised up 4.2% for CRDO's bottom line in the same period.
CRDO offers strong revenue growth prospects but customer concentration and execution risks remain concerns. COHR benefits from a broader optical portfolio, expanding manufacturing capacity and strong AI-driven demand, though rising capital expenditures could pressure cash flow.

Lumentum (LITE) revenue more than doubled to $1B while Coherent (COHR) grew 33% to $2B, both fueled by AI datacenter optical demand.
Lumentum's scarce high-power lasers pushed operating margins to 36.6%, but its 43x forward earnings valuation versus Coherent's 30x demands perfect execution.

Lumentum (NASDAQ:LITE) and Coherent (NYSE:COHR) both reported fiscal 2026 results in August with order books that reach into 2027 and beyond. Both sell into the copper-to-optical shift inside AI datacenters, so the useful question is which backlog has better terms.
Lumentum Runs Short of Lasers While Coherent Books Out 2027
Lumentum's quarter came down to scarcity. Management said it is "way behind our shipments" on high-power lasers because demand sped up faster than the production ramp. OCS shipments doubled from fiscal Q3, and non-GAAP operating margin reached 36.6%, up 2,160 bps YoY. That kind of margin jump usually means customers are paying up for parts they can't get anywhere else.
Coherent's story is variety. Datacenter and Communications brought in $1.615 billion, or 79% of revenue. Management described fiscal 2027 as "basically completely booked out," with orders reaching into calendar 2028. Industrial revenue of $430.5 million stayed roughly flat, and that drag is one the pure-play rival doesn't has.

Coherent Launches PhotonLink™ Integrated Optics Platform for AI Infrastructure
SAXONBURG, Pa., Sept. 21, 2026 (GLOBE NEWSWIRE) -- Coherent Corp. (NYSE: COHR), the global leader in photonics, today announced PhotonLink™, an integrated optics platform that brings together Coherent’s broad portfolio of critical photonics technologies, precision assembly and test capabilities to deliver complete optical solutions for next-generation AI datacenters. The platform supports co-packaged optics (CPO), near-packaged optics (NPO) and emerging chip to chip connectivity.
As AI systems continue to scale, demand for higher bandwidth and lower power is driving optical connectivity closer to compute and switching silicon. These architectures require lasers, silicon photonics, precision optics, fibers and detectors to work together. PhotonLink brings those technologies and the expertise to integrate them into one platform.
“The next leap in AI requires more than faster chips – it requires a new way to connect them,” said Jim Anderson, Chief Executive Officer at Coherent. “Customers need complete optical solutions, not just individual components. Coherent is uniquely positioned to bring together the critical technologies, integrate and test the finished assemblies, and manufacture them at scale. PhotonLink puts that capability to work for the next generation of AI infrastructure.”
Coherent’s vertical integration spans compound semiconductor materials, lasers, optics and specialty fiber through final assembly and test. PhotonLink gives customers access to both individual components and complete optical assemblies from one partner, helping simplify system design, streamline qualification and reduce the complexity of integrating technologies from multiple suppliers.
FROM CRITICAL TECHNOLOGIES TO COMPLETE OPTICAL ASSEMBLIES
The PhotonLink platform spans four functions of the optical path: Generate, Shape, Guide and Receive. The portfolio includes indium phosphide (InP) lasers, vertical-cavity surface-emitting laser (VCSEL) arrays, silicon photonics, isolators, specialty fibers, micro-optics and detectors. Coherent integrates these technologies into external laser sources, precision fiber assemblies and optical modules tailored to customer architectures.
CUSTOMER ENGAGEMENT AND MANUFACTURING SCALE
Coherent has more than ten CPO customer engagements and more than ten NPO engagements, with anchor customers and long-term agreements secured for both architectures. The company also has more than five engagements in emerging chip to chip connectivity. Revenue from the PhotonLink platform is expected to begin ramping in Q4 of CY2026.
PhotonLink builds on Coherent’s established datacenter manufacturing base, which has shipped more than 300 million InP lasers and more than one billion InP and gallium arsenide (GaAs) photodetectors. Coherent is expanding its 6” InP and specialty fiber manufacturing capacity to support the PhotonLink ramp.
Coherent hosted a PhotonLink launch event on September 21 at the Gran Hotel Miramar in Málaga during the European Conference on Optical Communication (ECOC) 2026. The presentation and webcast recording are available at PHOTONLINK™ Launch webcast
Visitors to ECOC 2026 can also meet Coherent experts and explore PhotonLink at Stand 2100, Hall 2, at FYCMA - Trade Fair & Congress Center in Málaga, Spain.
For more information about PhotonLink, visit https://www.coherent.com/datacenter-communications/photonlink
Coherent is the global photonics leader. We harness photons to drive innovation. Industry leaders in the datacenter, communications, and industrial markets rely on Coherent’s world-leading technology to fuel their own innovation and growth. Founded in 1971 and operating in more than 20 countries, Coherent brings the industry’s broadest, deepest technology stack; unmatched supply chain resilience; and global scale to help its customers solve their toughest technology challenges. For more information, visit coherent.com.
