From Loan Referrals to a Broader Financial Marketplace
Intuit Inc. (NASDAQ:INTU) added $441 million of Credit Karma revenue last year: $235 million from personal loans, $101 million from credit cards and $85 million from insurance. Lending supplied roughly 76% of incremental revenue; insurance contributed 19%. Diversification is advancing, but borrowing remains the main growth engine.
Intuit Inc. (NASDAQ:INTU) has products designed to encourage visits without another loan application. My Cards helps members manage existing card rewards, while Karma Drive uses driving data to identify insurance discounts. These services could reduce the cost of attracting returning customers and create referral opportunities. The test is whether customer benefits also improve shareholder economics. Revenue from additional visits must exceed product, marketing, and servicing costs.
Consolidated finances give Intuit Inc. (NASDAQ:INTU) room to invest. Fiscal 2026 operating cash flow reached $8.84 billion against $221 million of capital expenditure. It included a $2.06 billion stock-compensation addback. Credit Karma represented roughly 12% of group revenue, leaving accounting and tax products as substantial buffers.
Fiscal 2026 cash generation also benefited from lower cash-tax payments, including deductions for previously capitalized research spending. Management expects approximately $2 billion of cash taxes in fiscal 2027, so stronger operating earnings must help offset that higher cash outflow.
Revenue Diversification Must Survive Tighter Credit
For Intuit Inc. (NASDAQ:INTU), engagement and monetization can move in opposite directions. The Federal Reserve's July survey found tighter credit-card lending standards despite broadly unchanged demand. Credit Karma generally earns card and personal-loan referral fees when cards are issued or loans funded. Fewer approvals can therefore reduce revenue even with steady traffic. Compared with putting customer knowledge to work through direct lending, referrals make partners' willingness to approve and acquire borrowers central to revenue.
Insurance leads provide another revenue source without requiring new borrowing, but insurers can also cut acquisition budgets. Management's 11%–13% Credit Karma growth forecast for fiscal 2027 anticipates moderation. Investors need evidence that insurance revenue, repeat engagement, and conversion improve together. The combined Consumer segment's margin cannot isolate Credit Karma's profitability.
Intuit Inc. (NASDAQ:INTU) looks fairly valued at 13x forward P/E. Sustaining that judgment requires operating profit growth to absorb higher cash taxes while insurance and other services expand their contribution. Resilient referral conversion during tighter credit would strengthen the case for more dependable earnings. Continued dependence on loan growth would leave the diversification thesis unfinished.

Here's What You May Not Know About Analysts' Price Targets
According to researchers at several universities across the globe, a price target is one of many pieces of information about a stock that misleads investors far more often than it guides. In fact, empirical research shows that price targets set by several analysts, irrespective of the extent of agreement, rarely indicate where the price of a stock could actually be heading.
While Wall Street analysts have deep knowledge of a company's fundamentals and the sensitivity of its business to economic and industry issues, many of them tend to set overly optimistic price targets. Are you wondering why?
They usually do that to drum up interest in shares of companies that their firms either have existing business relationships with or are looking to be associated with. In other words, business incentives of firms covering a stock often result in inflated price targets set by analysts.
However, a tight clustering of price targets, which is represented by a low standard deviation, indicates that analysts have a high degree of agreement about the direction and magnitude of a stock's price movement. While that doesn't necessarily mean the stock will hit the average price target, it could be a good starting point for further research aimed at identifying the potential fundamental driving forces.
That said, while investors should not entirely ignore price targets, making an investment decision solely based on them could lead to disappointing ROI. So, price targets should always be treated with a high degree of skepticism.
There has been increasing optimism among analysts lately about the company's earnings prospects, as indicated by strong agreement among them in revising EPS estimates higher. How Investors Are Reacting To Intuit (INTU) Global AI Rollout
Mon, October 19, 2026 at 10:13 AM CDT 6 min read
Intuit has rolled out its Intuit Intelligence platform globally across QuickBooks and Intuit Accountant Suite, bringing AI driven automation, reporting and workflow tools to millions of small businesses and accounting firms, with features now in beta for international QuickBooks Online and QuickBooks Online Advanced customers.
Early user data from Intuit Intelligence points to meaningful productivity shifts, with reported monthly time savings for customers and more accountant hours redirected toward advisory work, which directly links the AI platform to how efficiently Intuit's products can be used in real firms.
We will look at how Intuit's investment narrative evolves as Intuit Intelligence expands globally and becomes embedded in accountant workflows.

To remain a shareholder in Intuit, you need to believe its AI-led system of intelligence across tax, small business, and mid-market products continues to deepen usage and support margin progress. The key short-term swing factor is whether Intuit Intelligence drives better customer engagement following recent softness in new customer additions and DIY tax share.
The biggest near-term risk is that lower-priced entry offers and Mailchimp simplification do not rebuild customer growth, leaving revenue and earnings below expectations. The international rollout of Intuit Intelligence appears additive to the core thesis, but it does not fundamentally change the fact that execution risk around customer acquisition remains central.
The extension of Intuit Intelligence across international QuickBooks and Intuit Accountant Suite ties directly into the existing AI catalyst that analysts have focused on. More workflows touched by automation can reinforce the value of QuickBooks, money and workforce solutions, and the Enterprise Suite for both small firms and mid-market clients.
The same announcement also highlights risk. With 10 million customers feeding the platform and complex AI workflows embedded in compliance-heavy products, any missteps in accuracy, transparency, or legal scrutiny around AI or marketing claims could affect costs and confidence. For you as an investor, execution quality on this global rollout is now a key factor to watch.
What The Current Intuit Forecasts Assume
Analysts are effectively asking you to underwrite a very specific path for Intuit as AI becomes more deeply woven into its tax and accounting workflows. The consensus view assumes revenue grows at 8.9% a year over the next few years and that profit margins step up from 21.3% today to 24.8% by year three. That margin lift, combined with steady share count reduction of about 4.01% a year, underpins forecasts that earnings move from US$4.6b today to US$6.9b by 2029, while the stock trades on a P/E of 18x those projected profits compared with 16.1x on current earnings.
On these numbers, the implied valuation for Intuit also rests on where you think it should sit relative to the wider US software group. The consensus view uses a future P/E that is below the reported 29.7x for the industry, even as analysts model higher margins and revenue expansion tied to Intuit Intelligence and the company's broader product ecosystem. That disconnect matters because it indicates expectations for operating performance are reasonably ambitious, but the implied P/E multiple is not at the very top of sector ranges based on the data provided.
Price targets bring these assumptions together into a single reference point for the stock. The average analyst target sits at US$405.60, which is 32% above the quoted share price of US$275.71, with a wide range from US$290 on the low end to US$732 at the high end. For you as a shareholder or prospective investor, the key test is whether the AI led growth story and the shift in customer acquisition tactics make the path to US$27.7b of revenue and US$6.9b of earnings by 2029 feel realistic enough for that target to be a useful benchmark.
Intuit's current consensus outlook points to revenues of US$27.7b and earnings of US$6.9b by 2029, built on 8.9% yearly revenue growth and an earnings increase of about US$2.3b from US$4.6b today.

Their AI adoption worries create a far more cautious story. With the international launch now public, you can expect those views to evolve. Intuit to Acquire Sequence to Boost AI-Powered Mid-Market Offerings
Mon, October 19, 2026 at 7:20 AM CDT 2 min read
Intuit Inc. INTU has announced an agreement to acquire Sequence, an AI-native revenue management platform, to expand its capabilities in the mid-market enterprise resource planning (ERP) space. The acquisition is expected to strengthen Intuit Enterprise Suite and QuickBooks Online Advanced by integrating automated quote-to-revenue workflows, including pricing, billing, collections and revenue recognition. The move aligns with Intuit's strategy to attract growing businesses seeking alternatives to traditional ERP solutions offered by Oracle ORCL and SAP SAP.
Sequence's platform replaces manual billing processes and spreadsheets with AI-powered automation, supporting complex revenue models based on consumption, usage, seats and milestones. These capabilities could help Intuit expand into industries such as B2B software and professional services, where hybrid pricing structures are becoming increasingly common. By simplifying revenue management and reducing administrative workloads, Intuit could improve customer retention and attract businesses that might otherwise consider more established enterprise solutions from Oracle and SAP.
The acquisition also strengthens Intuit's positioning in an increasingly competitive market for AI-enabled financial software. Oracle offers integrated subscription and revenue management capabilities through its cloud applications, while SAP provides subscription billing and revenue recognition solutions within its enterprise software ecosystem.
Intuit's strategy of combining AI-native automation with its existing financial management platform could help differentiate its offerings among mid-market customers seeking simpler and more integrated solutions. Sequence's AI engineering expertise could accelerate product innovation and support Intuit's ambition to develop a comprehensive AI-native ERP platform.
The acquisition could create cross-selling opportunities across Intuit's existing customer base while expanding its addressable market in more complex business segments. While competition from Oracle and SAP remains significant, the addition of Sequence could reinforce Intuit's long-term growth prospects by broadening its mid-market capabilities and strengthening its AI-driven financial software ecosystem.

Building Wealth Across More Than Just the Market
Building a resilient portfolio means thinking beyond a single asset or market trend. Economic cycles shift, sectors rise and fall, and no one investment performs well in every environment. That's why many investors look to diversify with platforms that provide access to real estate, fixed-income opportunities, precious metals, and even self-directed retirement accounts. By spreading exposure across multiple asset classes, it becomes easier to manage risk, capture steady returns, and create long-term wealth that isn't tied to the fortunes of just one company or industry.

Investors can buy fractional shares of single-family rentals and vacation homes starting with as little as $100. This allows everyday investors to diversify into real estate, collect rental income, and build long-term wealth without needing to manage properties directly.
Entertainment franchises can become valuable long-term assets when they successfully expand across multiple platforms. With more than 250 IPs in its portfolio and a strategy focused on retaining franchise rights while scaling successful stories across media, Skybound offers investors exposure to the growing entertainment and creator economy through a private company rather than traditional public market investments.
As artificial intelligence drives a surge in electricity demand, reliable power generation is becoming a critical part of the technology ecosystem. American PowerGen is developing natural gas-fired power plants in Texas, a fast-growing market fueled by AI data centers, manufacturing expansion, and population growth. By advancing projects through permitting, fuel supply, and grid interconnection, the company is positioning itself to help meet rising energy needs while offering investors exposure to the infrastructure supporting the next wave of AI and industrial growth.
As AI coding tools take on more of the work traditionally done by developers, companies are facing new challenges around code quality, context and the rising cost of AI-powered development. Founded by former PubMatic executives, Bito has raised more than $10 million from institutional and individual investors and is now raising additional capital through a Wefunder offering, giving investors an opportunity to invest in a company targeting an emerging need within the rapidly expanding AI software market.
For accredited investors looking beyond stocks and traditional real estate opportunities, DLP Capital provides access to private real estate strategies focused on workforce housing — homes for essential workers such as teachers, nurses, firefighters, and police officers. With more than $5.5 billion in assets under management and a community of 4,000+ accredited investors, DLP Capital gives investors access to real estate strategies designed around the growing need for housing that working Americans can actually afford.
Farmland has historically held its value through market volatility and delivered returns uncorrelated to stocks and bonds. For accredited investors, FarmTogether offers direct access to high-quality U.S. farmland starting at $15,000 — fully managed, with no landlord headaches.
Private real estate and private credit can add income and stability to a stock-heavy portfolio. Fundrise offers access to diversified private real estate and credit strategies through an easy-to-use platform, with professionally managed portfolios designed to generate passive income and long-term growth.

Strategic collaboration combines AI, data, and industry experience to transform how advisory services are delivered to scaling, more complex businesses
ATLANTA, Oct. 20, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- Aprio, the 20th largest business advisory and accounting firm in the U.S. today announced the next phase of a strategic partnership with Intuit, the global financial technology platform that makes TurboTax, Credit Karma, QuickBooks, Mailchimp, Intuit Enterprise Suite and Intuit Accountant Suite. The deepening partnership is designed to accelerate innovation across the accounting profession and help shape the future of AI-powered advisory and accounting services for mid-market businesses.
Aprio and Intuit will work together to develop AI-powered solutions designed to help identify tax planning opportunities, benchmark business performance, improve financial visibility, and support more informed decision-making across industries including construction, dental, wealth management and tax. Aprio's subject matter specialists will work alongside Intuit's product, engineering, and AI teams to turn real-world client needs into industry-specific capabilities that deliver greater visibility into business performance and enable more opportunities for advisors to focus on strategic guidance.
"Aprio's partners and advisors work alongside business owners every day, giving us a unique perspective on where growth is happening and where new opportunities are emerging," said Marc Silverman, Chief Commercial Officer, Aprio. "Together with Intuit, we're bringing those insights directly into the development of AI-powered solutions across tax, wealth management, dental and construction. By combining Aprio's industry experience with Intuit's technology and AI capabilities, we will shape tools that enable our professionals to spend more time helping clients pursue what's next."
"Delivering data-driven insights and leveraging AI to streamline accountant workflows enables them to drive and accelerate their clients' growth," said Travis Walter, SVP, Chief Sales Officer, Intuit. "Furthering our partnership with Aprio allows us to combine the power of their expertise with our financial technology platform so all firms have access to the products and services they need to deliver advisory services to their clients."
The partnership supports both organizations' commitment to innovation and the responsible application of artificial intelligence. By combining advanced technologies with deep advisory capabilities, Aprio and Intuit aim to help accelerate the evolution of accounting and advisory services and create new value across the business lifecycle. The collaboration builds on the strategic partnership announced in October 2025, when Aprio became Intuit's first advisory and accounting firm partner focused on accelerating mid-market business growth with client implementations of Intuit Enterprise Suite, Intuit's AI-native ERP for modern finance teams. This next phase expands the relationship beyond technology implementation to include AI innovation, industry-focused solutions, and new ways to help clients grow.
Intuit is the global financial technology platform that powers prosperity for consumers, businesses, and accountants, with products including TurboTax, Credit Karma, QuickBooks, Mailchimp, Intuit Enterprise Suite and Intuit Accountant Suite. Intuit's financial intelligence brings together decades of trusted data, deep financial expertise, AI, and human experts to help customers at every stage of their financial journey. This puts more money in their pockets, saves time by reducing manual work, and ensures they have complete confidence in every financial decision.
Aprio is redefining what it means to be a global advisory and accounting firm. We help businesses and individuals Account for Anything® — delivering clarity and confidence in a world full of unknowns. Aprio is the brand name under which Aprio, LLP, and Aprio Advisory Group, LLC deliver professional services to clients worldwide. Aprio Advisory Group, LLC provides advisory, tax, legal, wealth, and talent solutions to help build value, drive growth, manage risk, and protect wealth, while Aprio, LLP delivers audit and attest services with uncompromising quality and integrity. With more than 3,500 team members serving clients in 50+ countries and $5.8B in assets under advisement as of June 30, 2026, Aprio, the 20th largest business advisory and accounting firm in the U.S., is consistently recognized as a Top Workplace, celebrated for transformative growth on the Inc. 5000 and Inc. Power Partners lists, and led by Richard Kopelman, named to Accounting Today's Top 100 Most Influential People in Accounting. Learn more at Aprio.com.

Choosing between established software leaders requires balancing specialized fintech growth against broad enterprise cloud infrastructure. Investors must decide if Intuit (INTU +2.97%) or Oracle (ORCL +1.20%) offers the better value today.
Intuit dominates the personal tax and small business accounting landscape through its suite of financial tools. Oracle has pivoted from legacy databases to become a major force in cloud infrastructure and enterprise applications. Comparing them helps clarify whether you prefer a consumer-facing fintech powerhouse or an infrastructure backbone for large organizations.
Intuit focuses on financial technology for consumers and small businesses. Its ecosystem includes well-known brands like TurboTax and QuickBooks, serving roughly 93 million users worldwide. In its latest annual report, filed for FY 2025, the company highlighted how it relies on partnerships with third-party providers such as Amazon (AMZN +0.07%) for cloud services and distributes apps through platforms owned by Apple (AAPL -1.00%).
In FY 2026, revenue reached nearly $21.4 billion, representing a growth rate of approximately 13.9% over the previous year. This expansion helped the company achieve net income of close to $4.6 billion, yielding a net margin of about 21.3%. Net margin is a profitability ratio that shows what percentage of revenue remains as profit after all expenses are paid.
As of its July 2026 balance sheet, Intuit maintained a debt-to-equity ratio of roughly 0.4x. This ratio compares total debt to shareholder equity, with lower values typically indicating less reliance on borrowing. The current ratio was about 1.5x, which measures the ability to cover short-term debts with liquid assets. Free cash flow reached approximately $8.6 billion, though stock-based compensation represented roughly 23.3% of operating cash flow, which inflates reported cash generation since SBC is a non-cash expense added back in the cash flow statement.
Oracle provides a wide range of solutions among tech stocks, ranging from enterprise software to infrastructure services. Its business increasingly revolves around Oracle Cloud Infrastructure and cloud applications, serving government agencies and businesses in over 145 countries. In its latest annual report, the company noted strategic multicloud partnerships for interoperability with major competitors like Microsoft (MSFT -0.31%).
For FY 2026, the company reported revenue of close to $67.4 billion, a 17.4% increase compared to the prior year. Net income for the period was approximately $17.1 billion, resulting in a net margin of roughly 25.4%. This indicates a high level of profitability relative to its total sales volume over the fiscal period.
On its May 2026 balance sheet, Oracle reported a debt-to-equity ratio of nearly 3.7x. This indicates that total debt is significantly higher than the value of shareholder equity, reflecting a more leveraged position. The current ratio was approximately 1.1x, while free cash flow was a negative $23.7 billion due to heavy capital spending required to build out data centers.
Intuit faces intense competition from both large technology firms and low-cost tax software alternatives that might use artificial intelligence to disrupt traditional models. Its business is highly seasonal, with a significant portion of revenue tied to the U.S. tax season from November to April. Furthermore, the company manages sensitive financial data, making it a constant target for cyberattacks and data privacy concerns.
Oracle deals with significant risks regarding data privacy and recently faced a $115 million settlement related to its data broker activities. The company also faces stiff competition from industry leaders like Salesforce (CRM -0.01%) and SAP (SAP +1.30%) in the enterprise software market. Additionally, heavy reliance on sole-source suppliers for critical hardware components like AI accelerators creates potential vulnerabilities in its supply chain.
Intuit appears to trade at a lower P/S ratio and Forward P/E than Oracle based on sales over the past twelve months and future earnings estimates. The P/S ratio measures market value against sales over the past twelve months, while the Forward P/E compares price to future earnings estimates.
Valuation metrics sourced from Financial Modeling Prep (FMP) and may differ from other data providers.
Which stock would I buy in 2026?
I'd go with Oracle, though this is a more complicated pick than it first appears. Cloud infrastructure revenue more than doubled in the most recent quarter, total revenue grew at its fastest pace in years, and a backlog exceeding $600 billion signals demand stretching well into the future. Oracle is undoubtedly becoming one of the most important AI infrastructure companies in the world.
But it is worth understanding what comes with that. Oracle is spending aggressively to build data centers, which has pushed free cash flow negative and added significant debt to the balance sheet. A heavy reliance on OpenAI as a key customer adds concentration risk that investors should not overlook.
Intuit crossed $20 billion in annual revenue for the first time in the most recent quarter and keeps beating estimates. But slower growth guidance for the year ahead and valid concerns about AI disrupting its core tax and accounting businesses create uncertainty that is hard to dismiss.
Both stocks carry real risks. But Oracle's upside feels larger if the AI infrastructure build-out plays out as expected, and right now that's the better bet for a patient investor with a long horizon.

Intuit Offers Free Federal Tax Filing with Credit Karma Tax
Global financial technology company Intuit is re-launching Credit Karma Tax, providing users with free federal tax filing and a $15 flat rate for state filing, no matter their tax complexity.
Global financial technology company Intuit is re-launching Credit Karma Tax, providing users with free federal tax filing and a $15 flat rate for state filing, no matter their tax complexity.
In a media release on Oct. 20, Intuit says users of Credit Karma Tax “get a self-guided DIY experience with real-time AI help that simplifies the process throughout, tackling the majority of the manual work that filing often requires. AI-powered tools support members every step of the way, from giving them a head start by centralizing key financial data, then optimizing tax outcomes as they file, and delivering refunds faster, to building long-term financial health long after they submit their taxes.”
Before being bought by Intuit in 2020, Credit Karma offered a free, online tax preparation service that launched right before the 2017 filing season. But when Intuit was set to acquire Credit Karma, the U.S. Department of Justice required it to divest Credit Karma Tax to Square Inc. (now known as Block Inc.) in order for the $7.1 billion transaction to proceed.
Credit Karma to Offer Free Online Tax Preparation
The DOJ said at the time that without this divestiture, the Intuit/Credit Karma transaction “would substantially lessen competition for digital do-it-yourself tax preparation products.” Intuit is famously known as the maker of TurboTax.
“Intuit’s TurboTax has long led the market for digital do-it-yourself tax filing services, but disruptive competition from Credit Karma Tax has brought substantial benefits to American taxpayers,” Assistant Attorney General Makan Delrahim of the Justice Department’s Antitrust Division said in a statement on Nov. 25, 2020. “Today’s divestiture to Square, another highly successful and disruptive fintech company, ensures that taxpayers will continue to both benefit from this competition and benefit from new innovative financial service offerings from both Intuit and Square.”
But Credit Karma Tax is back, operating as a separate tax preparation offering from TurboTax.
“Today Credit Karma is so much more than a place to check your credit score; it’s delivering true financial confidence, where daily money management helps build the life our members want whether that’s affording a place to call home for their family, or planning a dream trip,” Mark Notarainni, executive vice president and general manager of the Consumer Group at Intuit, said in a statement on Oct. 20. “By adding transparent, free Federal filing specifically tailored to our members, no matter how complex their tax situation, we are expanding Credit Karma’s role as their daily AI-powered financial assistant, helping them strategically spend, save, and grow their money in one place.”
With Credit Karma already centralizing users’ financial data, including income, credit, cash flow, and taxes, all in one place, they already have a head start when tax time arrives, Intuit says. Filers can skip manual data entry by snapping a photo or automatically importing forms directly from employers or financial institutions, including stock sales and financial and crypto transactions. Credit Karma Tax will pre-fill the return using its comprehensive document checklist and gathering tools.
According to Intuit, Credit Karma Tax provides:
Tax prep and filing: Real-time help, gives clear explanations of return outcomes, and catches errors along the way using built-in AI tools like its expert chat function and, coming soon, Explanation and Error Agents.
Review and submission: Credit Karma Tax runs thousands of accuracy checks prior to submission to ensure compliance with IRS and state requirements. All returns are backed by a 100% accuracy guarantee. If a calculation error causes an IRS or state penalty, Intuit says it will cover the penalty and interest.
Completion and refund acceleration: Credit Karma transforms tax refund time into year-round financial planning through its suite of AI-powered financial tools. The Refund Agent turns refunds into actionable plans to pay down debt, save, or invest; the Debt Agent builds personalized paydown plans; and the Paycheck Agent allocates paychecks across bills, spending, and goals.
For this upcoming tax season, Credit Karma Tax provides accelerated access to funds:
Up to five days early: Access federal tax refunds up to five days early for free with deposit into a Credit Karma Checking account
Refund advance loan: With the upcoming launch of Credit Karma Tax’s tax year 2026 offering, apply for an up to $4,000 refund advance loan with $0 loan fees and 0% APR.
Credit Karma Tax is also offering the following paid add-ons:
Expert Support Bundle: Includes audit defense, ID protection benefits, 1:1 live product support, and the ability to pay the $15 state fee using a tax refund. ($29 at launch; pricing subject to change)
Expert Final Review: An option to add a final review by a tax expert to the Expert Support Bundle will also be available at launch. ($39 at launch; pricing subject to change)
Credit Karma Tax is available on the Credit Karma website and app. To become a member and create a free Credit Karma account visit creditkarma.com.

Home to many well-known brands including TurboTax, Credit Karma, Mailchimp and QuickBooks, Intuit is now aligning its various products under a central design ecosystem, with the aim that audiences will recognise that there is one trusted brand behind them all. It is also introducing a new website that tells the Intuit brand story for the first time.
“Over the past seven years, Intuit has evolved from a portfolio of individual products into one connected, AI-driven expert platform,” says JKR. “The rebrand makes that change visible: showing how Intuit products and technology come together to help customers put more money back in their pockets, save time, and make confident financial decisions.”
At the core of the new system is ‘Intuit Intelligence’, which is made up of Intuit AI and Intuit Experts, so customers always know when they’re interacting with AI, a human expert, or both. JKR has also introduced a new wordmark which aims “to feel more human, approachable, and ready for the AI-era”. It features a shortened ‘i’ logo, which is used across the brand experience, from app icons and product UI to large-scale brand executions.
The identity features a custom font, Tally, which was created in partnership with Jeremy Mickel of Mckl Type Foundry and is “designed to be hardworking with a human wink”. Tally’s shape also inspired a set of brand icons, which are used alongside bold illustration and vivid, high-contrast photography, plus a motion design system. The colour palette has also evolved, with Superblue being the lead and Blueberry unifying Intuit’s cornerstone brands, plus a secondary palette for added range and emphasis.
“Intuit has built enormous trust and equity across its individual products, but people don’t always connect that value back to the company behind them,” says JKR executive creative director Michael Ciancio. “When they do, research shows that trust in Intuit increases dramatically – and with it, their likelihood to explore and adopt more of its products.
“The new identity is designed to make that relationship visible: turning a portfolio of incredibly powerful brands into an ecosystem where each one can build equity for the others … and where Intuit itself becomes as recognisable and meaningful as the products it creates.”

Intuit, the American software company, has agreed to buy Sequence, a British financial technology business, in a deal estimated to be worth around $200m, according to a source close to the deal.
Intuit announced yesterday that it had signed an agreement to acquire Sequence, a business-to-business revenue management and billing platform founded in 2021. Intuit said the financial terms of the deal were not disclosed.
Riya Grover, Sequence’s co-founder and chief executive, holds a stake of more than 45 per cent in the company, according to the company database site Dun & Bradstreet, meaning she stands to make tens of millions of dollars from the sale. The deal is one of the largest exits by a UK artificial intelligence start-up led by a female co-founder.
The stories that matter to UK business, straight to your inbox.
“Revenue management has long been the most fragmented workflow in the back office. As businesses adopt usage-based and hybrid pricing, that complexity is only growing,” Grover, 38, said.
“We built Sequence to automate the entire process, from contract to revenue recognition, with AI agents automating daily tasks and working securely alongside finance teams. With Intuit’s platform and reach, and our shared alignment on serving mid-market businesses and creating AI-driven financial workflows, this is a natural fit for both companies.”
According to Intuit, the deal will give mid-market businesses and the accounting firms who advise them a single platform to price, bill and collect on revenue tied to consumption, usage, seats and milestones. The Nasdaq-listed company said Sequence would allow it to serve new industries, including business-to-business software and professional services.
“As businesses grow, pricing, billing, and collecting on complex usage-based and milestone-based revenue becomes one of the biggest reasons they choose an ERP,” said Ashley Still, executive vice president and general manager of Intuit’s Small Business and Mid-Market Group.
As part of the acquisition, Sequence employees, including Grover, will join Intuit in its mid-market product organisation. Intuit said it would continue to support Sequence’s customers after the acquisition closes and would develop an integrated offering in the coming months.
Grover co-founded the company with Eamon Jubbawy, 34, who previously co-founded Onfido, an ID verification software provider that was acquired by a US group in 2024 for $650m. Jubbawy owns a stake of more than 15 per cent in Sequence, according to Dun & Bradstreet.
The pair teamed up after seeing how much it cost companies selling to other businesses to build their own billing systems.
In 2022 Sequence raised $19m in its first funding round, backed by Andreessen Horowitz, the Silicon Valley venture capital firm known for its early bets on Airbnb, Facebook and Slack.
Grover sold her previous software business, Feedr, to Compass, the global catering group, in 2020 for a reported $24m.
Other significant UK AI software exits include Darktrace, which was acquired by the private equity firm Thoma Bravo in October 2024 for $5.3bn, and Faculty AI, which sold to Accenture this year for a reported $1bn.
Research from The ScaleUp Institute, an independent think tank, this month identified 333 women who had built businesses with revenues of more than £50m, up from 80 two years ago. The findings led campaigners to say “we are in the decade of the female founder.”
Business Matters reported in July that investors who have signed the Investing in Women Code had outperformed the wider market for a sixth year, while in May the British Business Bank committed £1m to co-invest with Angel Academe in female-led businesses.

Intuit Targets Complex Subscription Billing With Sequence Deal
The QuickBooks parent plans to acquire technology for managing custom contracts and usage-based billing, bringing subscription operations and accounting software closer together.
Intuit, the company behind QuickBooks, announced October 15 that it has agreed to acquire Sequence, a software company that helps businesses manage customer contracts, billing, collections and revenue accounting.
The acquisition would expand Intuit's ability to serve businesses whose revenue doesn't fit neatly into a standard monthly or annual subscription. Sequence handles arrangements involving customer seats, usage charges, minimum spending commitments and individually negotiated terms.
For subscription operators, the news points to a potential shift in the technology market. Large financial software companies are moving further into work traditionally handled by specialized subscription billing and revenue management systems.
A software company might sell annual subscriptions to business customers, with some paying a fixed fee and others paying according to the number of employees using the product. Larger customers may have negotiated agreements that combine minimum commitments with additional usage charges.
When customers add seats, change their usage or renegotiate terms, the billing system has to keep up. The next invoice needs to reflect what was agreed, while finance needs accurate records of what has been billed, collected and earned.
Sequence is designed to handle those different arrangements. Its platform connects customer contracts to billing schedules, calculates charges based on agreed terms, prepares invoices and helps manage collections. It also supports revenue recognition, the accounting process for recording revenue as a company earns it.
Sequence already connects with QuickBooks and other accounting systems. Intuit plans to go further by bringing Sequence's capabilities into its own mid-market products, including Intuit Enterprise Suite and QuickBooks Online Advanced.
The acquisition has not yet closed, and the companies haven't disclosed the purchase price. Intuit says it will continue supporting existing Sequence customers after the deal closes and plans to develop an integrated offering in the coming months. Future product pricing and availability haven't been announced.
Sequence uses AI agents to help finance teams with work that often requires manual attention. Its software can read signed contracts, identify pricing terms, prepare billing information and draft reminders for overdue invoices. It can also assist with matching payments to outstanding invoices.
Sequence draws a distinction between what its AI agents do and how customer charges are calculated. The company says AI does not calculate the amounts customers owe. Instead, its billing engine uses defined pricing rules and contract terms to produce charges that can be checked and reproduced. Sequence also describes controls that allow finance teams to review and approve work performed by its AI agents.
For subscription operators, that approach addresses a practical concern. When customers question an invoice, the business needs to explain where the charge came from, particularly when pricing involves changing usage, discounts or adjustments during a contract.
Intuit hasn't yet explained how Sequence's AI capabilities will appear in its own products.
Financial Software Companies Move Further Into Recurring Revenue
Intuit isn't the only major financial technology company expanding into specialized billing technology.
In January, Stripe completed its acquisition of Metronome, which provides technology for managing usage-based, subscription and hybrid billing models. Both acquisitions point to growing interest among larger financial technology companies in the systems businesses use to manage recurring revenue.
Companies with complex pricing often rely on a combination of specialized billing platforms, accounting software and spreadsheets. Keeping customer agreements, invoices and financial records consistent across those systems can take considerable work.
Intuit's move could eventually give companies with complex billing needs another option for managing contracts, charges and financial records within the same platform. Whether that approach is a better fit than a specialized billing provider will depend on the company's pricing arrangements, operating needs and the capabilities of the eventual product.
For years, subscription billing and accounting have been treated as separate jobs. Billing systems manage what customers owe under their subscriptions and contracts. Accounting systems record the financial results. Intuit's planned acquisition of Sequence suggests that separation may be changing.
Stripe's acquisition of Metronome earlier this year points in a similar direction. Large financial technology companies are moving deeper into the systems that manage recurring revenue, an area where specialized subscription billing providers have traditionally played a central role.
For subscription operators, the bigger question is whether billing technology will increasingly become part of a company's broader financial software decision. That could change who chooses the systems, how they work together and how much control subscription teams have over the tools they depend on.
There are potential advantages to bringing billing and accounting closer together, particularly when customer contracts and pricing change frequently. But a financial platform still has to handle the exceptions that make subscription billing difficult. A customer adding seats halfway through a contract or disputing a usage charge needs an accurate answer, regardless of which company supplies the software.
Intuit hasn't said how it will price or package Sequence's capabilities, and the acquisition hasn't closed. We don't yet know whether the combined offering will be a better alternative to established subscription billing platforms. But if accounting platforms begin taking on more responsibility for subscription billing, operators may find that decisions affecting their customer relationships are increasingly tied to choices made elsewhere in the business.
Intuit's planned acquisition of Sequence raises a question for subscription operators: if billing becomes part of a broader financial platform, who makes the technology decisions, and how are the subscription team's needs protected? INTU vs. MSFT: Which Stock Is the Better Value Option?

Intuit (INTU): Can Credit Karma Grow Beyond the Lending Cycle?
Tue, October 20, 2026 at 8:49 AM CDT 4 min read
Intuit Inc. (NASDAQ:INTU), featured among Insider Monkey's 10 Best Software Stocks to Buy in 2026, has a growing financial marketplace inside its software business. Credit Karma revenue rose 20% to $2.64 billion in fiscal 2026. As banks tighten credit-card standards, insurance offers another way to grow. Yet personal loans and credit cards still generated most of the increase.
Intuit Inc. (NASDAQ:INTU) has a 13x forward P/E and an 18x trailing P/E. Trailing P/E uses past earnings, while forward P/E uses forecast earnings. Management separately projects fiscal 2027 GAAP EPS growth of 22%–24%. The forward valuation looks provisionally reasonable if stronger earnings support cash generation after higher tax payments.
The forward P/E was 35x in July 2025. Intuit Inc. (NASDAQ:INTU) now expects revenue growth of 9%–10%, versus 14% last year, supporting a more moderate valuation. Management also now includes stock compensation in adjusted earnings. That makes the distinction between operating progress and accounting adjustments important when assessing its guidance.
H&R Block, Inc. (NYSE:HRB), a close tax-preparation comparison, has a 7x forward P/E. Intuit Inc. (NASDAQ:INTU) guides to non-GAAP EPS growth of 23%–24% under its revised definition for the fiscal year ending July 2027, versus approximately 14%–18% for its rival's June 2027 year. Faster growth and recurring business-software revenue support a premium over a business more dependent on seasonal tax preparation.
Also read: 10 Best Undervalued Stocks to Buy in October
TD Cowen Expects Strong Q3 Performance from Intuit (INTU)
From Loan Referrals to a Broader Financial Marketplace
Intuit Inc. (NASDAQ:INTU) added $441 million of Credit Karma revenue last year: $235 million from personal loans, $101 million from credit cards and $85 million from insurance. Lending supplied roughly 76% of incremental revenue; insurance contributed 19%. Diversification is advancing, but borrowing remains the main growth engine.
Intuit Inc. (NASDAQ:INTU) has products designed to encourage visits without another loan application. My Cards helps members manage existing card rewards, while Karma Drive uses driving data to identify insurance discounts. These services could reduce the cost of attracting returning customers and create referral opportunities. The test is whether customer benefits also improve shareholder economics. Revenue from additional visits must exceed product, marketing, and servicing costs.
Consolidated finances give Intuit Inc. (NASDAQ:INTU) room to invest. Fiscal 2026 operating cash flow reached $8.84 billion against $221 million of capital expenditure. It included a $2.06 billion stock-compensation addback. Credit Karma represented roughly 12% of group revenue, leaving accounting and tax products as substantial buffers.
Fiscal 2026 cash generation also benefited from lower cash-tax payments, including deductions for previously capitalized research spending. Management expects approximately $2 billion of cash taxes in fiscal 2027, so stronger operating earnings must help offset that higher cash outflow.
Revenue Diversification Must Survive Tighter Credit
For Intuit Inc. (NASDAQ:INTU), engagement and monetization can move in opposite directions. The Federal Reserve's July survey found tighter credit-card lending standards despite broadly unchanged demand. Credit Karma generally earns card and personal-loan referral fees when cards are issued or loans funded. Fewer approvals can therefore reduce revenue even with steady traffic. Compared with putting customer knowledge to work through direct lending, referrals make partners' willingness to approve and acquire borrowers central to revenue.
Insurance leads provide another revenue source without requiring new borrowing, but insurers can also cut acquisition budgets. Management's 11%–13% Credit Karma growth forecast for fiscal 2027 anticipates moderation. Investors need evidence that insurance revenue, repeat engagement, and conversion improve together. The combined Consumer segment's margin cannot isolate Credit Karma's profitability.
Intuit Inc. (NASDAQ:INTU) looks fairly valued at 13x forward P/E. Sustaining that judgment requires operating profit growth to absorb higher cash taxes while insurance and other services expand their contribution. Resilient referral conversion during tighter credit would strengthen the case for more dependable earnings. Continued dependence on loan growth would leave the diversification thesis unfinished.
While we acknowledge the risk and potential of INTU as an investment, our conviction lies in the belief that some AI stocks hold greater promise for delivering higher returns and doing so within a shorter time frame. Intuit Launches Credit Karma Tax: Free Federal Filing With Faster Refunds, Expanding Its Daily AI-Powered Financial Assistance

Combines Free, $0 Federal, and flat-rate, $15* State filing, regardless of your tax complexity, with refunds up to 5 days early for free through Credit Karma
AI-powered support before, during and after tax season, alongside daily financial tools deliver less work, simplified filing and financial confidence to members
MOUNTAIN VIEW, Calif., October 20, 2026--(BUSINESS WIRE)--Intuit Inc. (Nasdaq: INTU), the global financial technology platform that makes TurboTax, Credit Karma, QuickBooks, Mailchimp, Intuit Enterprise Suite, and Intuit Accountant Suite, today announced the launch of Credit Karma Tax offering a simple, flat-rate pricing model of free, $0 federal and flat-rate, $15 state filing to all members, no matter their tax complexity. Credit Karma, a daily financial assistant, combines transparent pricing, faster access to refunds and financial confidence all in one place. With Credit Karma Tax, members get a self-guided DIY experience with real-time AI help that simplifies the process throughout, tackling the majority of the manual work that filing often requires. AI-powered tools support members every step of the way, from giving them a head start by centralizing key financial data, then optimizing tax outcomes as they file, and delivering refunds faster, to building long-term financial health long after they submit their taxes.
"Today Credit Karma is so much more than a place to check your credit score; it's delivering true financial confidence, where daily money management helps build the life our members want whether that's affording a place to call home for their family, or planning a dream trip," said Mark Notarainni, Executive Vice President and General Manager, Consumer Group, Intuit. "By adding transparent, free Federal filing specifically tailored to our members, no matter how complex their tax situation, we are expanding Credit Karma's role as their daily AI-powered financial assistant, helping them strategically spend, save, and grow their money in one place."
Centralized Data Delivers Unmatched Speed and Convenience
Credit Karma is already part of millions of consumers' daily financial routines. By centralizing a member's financial data, including income, credit, cash flow and taxes all in one place, when tax time arrives, Credit Karma members already have a head start. Filers can skip manual data entry by simply snapping a photo or automatically importing forms directly from employers or financial institutions, including stock sales, and financial and crypto transactions. Credit Karma Tax will pre-fill the return, and with its comprehensive document checklist and gathering tools, the guesswork is removed from filing.
File & Achieve Financial Progress with Confidence: Accuracy Guaranteed, AI Assistance, and Refunds Directed Toward Money Goals
From the moment members start filing to the moment their refund lands, Credit Karma Tax utilizes Intuit's domain expertise, AI and platform technology to get it right and make that money work harder for them.
Tax Prep & Filing: Credit Karma Tax provides real-time help, gives clear explanations of return outcomes, and catches errors along the way using built-in AI tools like its expert chat function and, coming soon, Explanation and Error Agents.
Review & Submission: Credit Karma Tax runs thousands of accuracy checks prior to submission to ensure compliance with IRS and state requirements. All returns are backed by a 100% accuracy guarantee. If a calculation error causes an IRS or state penalty, Intuit covers the penalty and interest.
Completion & Refund Acceleration: Credit Karma Tax doesn't stop at filing. Tax refunds are often the single biggest financial event of the year for Americans. Credit Karma transforms that moment into year-round financial health through its suite of AI-powered financial tools. The Refund Agent turns refunds into actionable plans to pay down debt, save, or invest; the Debt Agent builds personalized paydown plans saving members $200+ a month; and the Paycheck Agent allocates paychecks across bills, spending, and goals.
With 70% of Americans relying on tax refunds to cover basic living expenses, for this upcoming tax season Credit Karma Tax provides accelerated access to funds:
Up to 5 Days Early: Access federal tax refunds up to 5 days early for free with deposit into a Credit Karma Checking account.1
Refund Advance Loan: With the upcoming launch of Credit Karma Tax's Tax Year 2026 offering, apply for an up to a $4,000 Refund Advance loan with $0 loan fees and 0% APR.1
Credit Karma Tax offers a predictable, flat-rate pricing structure, regardless of tax complexity, with no hidden fees: $0 Federal Filing, $15 per State Filing.
For filers seeking added peace of mind or expert support as they file their 2026 taxes, Credit Karma Tax offers straightforward paid add-ons:
Expert Support Bundle: Includes audit defense, ID protection benefits, 1:1 live product support, and the ability to pay the $15 state fee using a tax refund. ($29 at launch. Pricing subject to change)¹.
Expert Final Review: An option to add a final review by a tax expert to the above bundle will also be available at launch. ($39 at launch. Pricing subject to change)¹.
Operating as a distinct, streamlined tax preparation offering, Credit Karma Tax is available on the Credit Karma website and app. To become a member and create a free Credit Karma account visit creditkarma.com.

Wall Street Analysts Think Intuit (INTU) Could Surge 26.36%: Read This Before Placing a Bet
Tue, October 20, 2026 at 7:55 AM CDT 4 min read
Intuit (INTU) closed the last trading session at $325.62, gaining 7.1% over the past four weeks, but there could be plenty of upside left in the stock if short-term price targets set by Wall Street analysts are any guide. The mean price target of $411.45 indicates a 26.4% upside potential.
The average comprises 31 short-term price targets ranging from a low of $290.00 to a high of $900.00, with a standard deviation of $126.65. While the lowest estimate indicates a decline of 10.9% from the current price level, the most optimistic estimate points to a 176.4% upside. More than the range, one should note the standard deviation here, as it helps understand the variability of the estimates. The smaller the standard deviation, the greater the agreement among analysts.
While the consensus price target is a much-coveted metric for investors, solely banking on this metric to make an investment decision may not be wise at all. That's because the ability and unbiasedness of analysts in setting price targets have long been questionable.
However, an impressive consensus price target is not the only factor that indicates a potential upside in INTU. This view is strengthened by the agreement among analysts that the company will report better earnings than what they estimated earlier. Though a positive trend in earnings estimate revisions doesn't give any idea as to how much the stock could surge, it has proven effective in predicting an upside.
Zacks Price, Consensus and EPS Surprise Chart for INTU
Here's What You May Not Know About Analysts' Price Targets
According to researchers at several universities across the globe, a price target is one of many pieces of information about a stock that misleads investors far more often than it guides. In fact, empirical research shows that price targets set by several analysts, irrespective of the extent of agreement, rarely indicate where the price of a stock could actually be heading.
While Wall Street analysts have deep knowledge of a company's fundamentals and the sensitivity of its business to economic and industry issues, many of them tend to set overly optimistic price targets. Are you wondering why?
They usually do that to drum up interest in shares of companies that their firms either have existing business relationships with or are looking to be associated with. In other words, business incentives of firms covering a stock often result in inflated price targets set by analysts.
However, a tight clustering of price targets, which is represented by a low standard deviation, indicates that analysts have a high degree of agreement about the direction and magnitude of a stock's price movement. While that doesn't necessarily mean the stock will hit the average price target, it could be a good starting point for further research aimed at identifying the potential fundamental driving forces.
That said, while investors should not entirely ignore price targets, making an investment decision solely based on them could lead to disappointing ROI. So, price targets should always be treated with a high degree of skepticism.
There has been increasing optimism among analysts lately about the company's earnings prospects, as indicated by strong agreement among them in revising EPS estimates higher. And that could be a legitimate reason to expect an upside in the stock. After all, empirical research shows a strong correlation between trends in earnings estimate revisions and near-term stock price movements.
Over the last 30 days, the Zacks Consensus Estimate for the current year has increased 0%, as one estimate has moved higher compared to no negative revision.
Moreover, INTU currently has a Zacks Rank #2 (Buy), which means it is in the top 20% of more than 4,000 stocks that we rank based on four factors related to earnings estimates. Given an impressive externally-audited track record, this is a more conclusive indication of the stock's potential upside in the near term. You can see the complete list of today's Zacks Rank #1 (Strong Buy) stocks here >>>> .
Therefore, while the consensus price target may not be a reliable indicator of how much INTU could gain, the direction of price movement it implies does appear to be a good guide.

How Investors Are Reacting To Intuit (INTU) Global AI Rollout
Mon, October 19, 2026 at 10:13 AM CDT 6 min read
Intuit has rolled out its Intuit Intelligence platform globally across QuickBooks and Intuit Accountant Suite, bringing AI driven automation, reporting and workflow tools to millions of small businesses and accounting firms, with features now in beta for international QuickBooks Online and QuickBooks Online Advanced customers.
Early user data from Intuit Intelligence points to meaningful productivity shifts, with reported monthly time savings for customers and more accountant hours redirected toward advisory work, which directly links the AI platform to how efficiently Intuit's products can be used in real firms.
We will look at how Intuit's investment narrative evolves as Intuit Intelligence expands globally and becomes embedded in accountant workflows.
Spot other AI focused opportunities that are moving accounting and back office workflows forward by scanning the hand picked 39 profitable AI stocks that aren't just burning cash that are already turning automation into real revenue.
To remain a shareholder in Intuit, you need to believe its AI-led system of intelligence across tax, small business, and mid-market products continues to deepen usage and support margin progress. The key short-term swing factor is whether Intuit Intelligence drives better customer engagement following recent softness in new customer additions and DIY tax share.
The biggest near-term risk is that lower-priced entry offers and Mailchimp simplification do not rebuild customer growth, leaving revenue and earnings below expectations. The international rollout of Intuit Intelligence appears additive to the core thesis, but it does not fundamentally change the fact that execution risk around customer acquisition remains central.
The extension of Intuit Intelligence across international QuickBooks and Intuit Accountant Suite ties directly into the existing AI catalyst that analysts have focused on. More workflows touched by automation can reinforce the value of QuickBooks, money and workforce solutions, and the Enterprise Suite for both small firms and mid-market clients.
The same announcement also highlights risk. With 10 million customers feeding the platform and complex AI workflows embedded in compliance-heavy products, any missteps in accuracy, transparency, or legal scrutiny around AI or marketing claims could affect costs and confidence. For you as an investor, execution quality on this global rollout is now a key factor to watch.
What The Current Intuit Forecasts Assume
Analysts are effectively asking you to underwrite a very specific path for Intuit as AI becomes more deeply woven into its tax and accounting workflows. The consensus view assumes revenue grows at 8.9% a year over the next few years and that profit margins step up from 21.3% today to 24.8% by year three. That margin lift, combined with steady share count reduction of about 4.01% a year, underpins forecasts that earnings move from US$4.6b today to US$6.9b by 2029, while the stock trades on a P/E of 18x those projected profits compared with 16.1x on current earnings.
On these numbers, the implied valuation for Intuit also rests on where you think it should sit relative to the wider US software group. The consensus view uses a future P/E that is below the reported 29.7x for the industry, even as analysts model higher margins and revenue expansion tied to Intuit Intelligence and the company's broader product ecosystem. That disconnect matters because it indicates expectations for operating performance are reasonably ambitious, but the implied P/E multiple is not at the very top of sector ranges based on the data provided.
Price targets bring these assumptions together into a single reference point for the stock. The average analyst target sits at US$405.60, which is 32% above the quoted share price of US$275.71, with a wide range from US$290 on the low end to US$732 at the high end. For you as a shareholder or prospective investor, the key test is whether the AI led growth story and the shift in customer acquisition tactics make the path to US$27.7b of revenue and US$6.9b of earnings by 2029 feel realistic enough for that target to be a useful benchmark.
Intuit's current consensus outlook points to revenues of US$27.7b and earnings of US$6.9b by 2029, built on 8.9% yearly revenue growth and an earnings increase of about US$2.3b from US$4.6b today.

The biggest contrast comes from how much weight you put on AI execution risk. While the consensus expects Intuit Intelligence to support that US$27.7b revenue and US$6.9b earnings path by 2029, the lowest analysts were working off roughly US$27.3b and US$6.5b. Their AI adoption worries create a far more cautious story. With the international launch now public, you can expect those views to evolve. Treat this as your cue to explore both sides rather than lean on a single forecast.

Intuit to Acquire Sequence to Boost AI-Powered Mid-Market Offerings
Mon, October 19, 2026 at 7:20 AM CDT 2 min read
Intuit Inc. INTU has announced an agreement to acquire Sequence, an AI-native revenue management platform, to expand its capabilities in the mid-market enterprise resource planning (ERP) space. The acquisition is expected to strengthen Intuit Enterprise Suite and QuickBooks Online Advanced by integrating automated quote-to-revenue workflows, including pricing, billing, collections and revenue recognition. The move aligns with Intuit's strategy to attract growing businesses seeking alternatives to traditional ERP solutions offered by Oracle ORCL and SAP SAP.
Sequence's platform replaces manual billing processes and spreadsheets with AI-powered automation, supporting complex revenue models based on consumption, usage, seats and milestones. These capabilities could help Intuit expand into industries such as B2B software and professional services, where hybrid pricing structures are becoming increasingly common. By simplifying revenue management and reducing administrative workloads, Intuit could improve customer retention and attract businesses that might otherwise consider more established enterprise solutions from Oracle and SAP.
The acquisition also strengthens Intuit's positioning in an increasingly competitive market for AI-enabled financial software. Oracle offers integrated subscription and revenue management capabilities through its cloud applications, while SAP provides subscription billing and revenue recognition solutions within its enterprise software ecosystem.
Intuit's strategy of combining AI-native automation with its existing financial management platform could help differentiate its offerings among mid-market customers seeking simpler and more integrated solutions. Sequence's AI engineering expertise could accelerate product innovation and support Intuit's ambition to develop a comprehensive AI-native ERP platform.
The acquisition could create cross-selling opportunities across Intuit's existing customer base while expanding its addressable market in more complex business segments. While competition from Oracle and SAP remains significant, the addition of Sequence could reinforce Intuit's long-term growth prospects by broadening its mid-market capabilities and strengthening its AI-driven financial software ecosystem.

Intuit Bets on AI-Powered Revenue Automation with Sequence Acquisition
The word INTUIT is displayed in blue capital letters on a white smartphone screen, against a blurred pink and purple background. (Credit: Photo: PJ McDonnell/Shutterstock)
Sun, October 18, 2026 at 4:30 PM CDT 6 min read
Benzinga and Yahoo Finance LLC may earn commission or revenue on some items through the links below.
Intuit Inc. stock is trading higher by more than 6% on Thursday after the company announced to acquire Sequence, an AI-native revenue management platform.
The acquisition expands Intuit's revenue management offerings for mid-market businesses.
Founded in 2021, Sequence leverages AI to help B2B finance and commercial teams automate the full quote-to-revenue lifecycle, including deal configuration and pricing, billing, invoicing, collections, and revenue recognition.

The acquisition will strengthen the capabilities of Intuit's Intuit Enterprise Suite, a resource planning and consolidation platform, and QuickBooks Online Advanced, its cloud-based accounting platform.
The acquisition will also expand Intuit's reach to sectors, including B2B software, professional services, construction, healthcare, and manufacturing.
Sequence co-founder and CEO Riya Grover highlighted the growing need for revenue management automation as business complexity grows with usage-based and hybrid pricing revenue models.
Ashley Still, executive vice president and general manager, Small Business & Mid-Market Group at Intuit, said the acquisition further extends Intuit Enterprise Suite directly into industries that increasingly leverage AI consumption models and is a meaningful step forward for the company to deliver AI-native ERP for complex businesses.
Following the acquisition, Grover and the Sequence team will join Intuit's Mid-Market product organization.
Intuit held $4.7 billion in cash and cash equivalents and had total debt of $7.7 billion as of July 31.
Financial terms of the deal were not disclosed.

Intuit Reiterates First Quarter and Full Year Fiscal 2027 Guidance
Intuit reiterated its financial guidance for the first quarter and full year fiscal 2027 in conjunction with its Investor Day on Sept. 17.
Intuit expects fiscal 2027 revenue to be between $23.279 billion and $23.512 billion, representing 9% to 10% growth.
GAAP EPS is projected at $20.12 to $20.36, while adjusted EPS is expected at $22.88 to $23.12, compared with the analyst consensus estimate of $24.04.
The company expects first-quarter fiscal 2027 revenues between $4.29 billion to $4.31 billion and adjusted EPS at $2.44 to $2.48.

Building Wealth Across More Than Just the Market
Building a resilient portfolio means thinking beyond a single asset or market trend. Economic cycles shift, sectors rise and fall, and no one investment performs well in every environment. That's why many investors look to diversify with platforms that provide access to real estate, fixed-income opportunities, precious metals, and even self-directed retirement accounts. By spreading exposure across multiple asset classes, it becomes easier to manage risk, capture steady returns, and create long-term wealth that isn't tied to the fortunes of just one company or industry.
For accredited investors looking beyond stocks and bonds, EquityMultiple provides access to vetted commercial real estate deals starting at $5,000, with only ~5% of opportunities passing their due diligence process.
Backed by Jeff Bezos, Arrived Homes makes real estate investing accessible with a low barrier to entry. Investors can buy fractional shares of single-family rentals and vacation homes starting with as little as $100. This allows everyday investors to diversify into real estate, collect rental income, and build long-term wealth without needing to manage properties directly.
Entertainment franchises can become valuable long-term assets when they successfully expand across multiple platforms. Skybound Entertainment, the company behind The Walking Dead and Invincible, develops original intellectual property that spans comics, television, film, video games, merchandise, and licensing. With more than 250 IPs in its portfolio and a strategy focused on retaining franchise rights while scaling successful stories across media, Skybound offers investors exposure to the growing entertainment and creator economy through a private company rather than traditional public market investments.
As artificial intelligence drives a surge in electricity demand, reliable power generation is becoming a critical part of the technology ecosystem. American PowerGen is developing natural gas-fired power plants in Texas, a fast-growing market fueled by AI data centers, manufacturing expansion, and population growth. By advancing projects through permitting, fuel supply, and grid interconnection, the company is positioning itself to help meet rising energy needs while offering investors exposure to the infrastructure supporting the next wave of AI and industrial growth.
As AI coding tools take on more of the work traditionally done by developers, companies are facing new challenges around code quality, context and the rising cost of AI-powered development. Bito is building software designed to help AI coding agents better understand complex codebases while helping companies control AI development costs. Founded by former PubMatic executives, Bito has raised more than $10 million from institutional and individual investors and is now raising additional capital through a Wefunder offering, giving investors an opportunity to invest in a company targeting an emerging need within the rapidly expanding AI software market.
For accredited investors looking beyond stocks and traditional real estate opportunities, DLP Capital provides access to private real estate strategies focused on workforce housing — homes for essential workers such as teachers, nurses, firefighters, and police officers. With more than $5.5 billion in assets under management and a community of 4,000+ accredited investors, DLP Capital gives investors access to real estate strategies designed around the growing need for housing that working Americans can actually afford.
Farmland has historically held its value through market volatility and delivered returns uncorrelated to stocks and bonds. For accredited investors, FarmTogether offers direct access to high-quality U.S. farmland starting at $15,000 — fully managed, with no landlord headaches.
Private real estate and private credit can add income and stability to a stock-heavy portfolio. Fundrise offers access to diversified private real estate and credit strategies through an easy-to-use platform, with professionally managed portfolios designed to generate passive income and long-term growth.

text: Strategic collaboration combines AI, data, and industry experience to transform how advisory services are delivered to scaling, more complex businesses ATLANTA, Oct. 20, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- Aprio, the 20th largest business advisory and accounting firm in the U.S. today announced the next phase of a strategic partnership with Intuit, the global financial technology platform that makes TurboTax, Credit Karma, QuickBooks, Mailchimp, Intuit Enterprise Suite and Intuit Accountant Suite. The deepening partnership is designed to accelerate innovation across the accounting profession and help shape the future of AI-powered advisory and accounting services for mid-market businesses. Aprio and Intuit will work together to develop AI-powered solutions designed to help identify tax planning opportunities, benchmark business performance, improve financial visibility, and support more informed decision-making across industries including construction, dental, wealth management and tax. Aprio's subject matter specialists will work alongside Intuit's product, engineering, and AI teams to turn real-world client needs into industry-specific capabilities that deliver greater visibility into business performance and enable more opportunities for advisors to focus on strategic guidance. "Aprio's partners and advisors work alongside business owners every day, giving us a unique perspective on where growth is happening and where new opportunities are emerging," said Marc Silverman, Chief Commercial Officer, Aprio. "Together with Intuit, we're bringing those insights directly into the development of AI-powered solutions across tax, wealth management, dental and construction. By combining Aprio's industry experience with Intuit's technology and AI capabilities, we will shape tools that enable our professionals to spend more time helping clients pursue what's next." "Delivering data-driven insights and leveraging AI to streamline accountant workflows enables them to drive and accelerate their clients' growth," said Travis Walter, SVP, Chief Sales Officer, Intuit. "Furthering our partnership with Aprio allows us to combine the power of their expertise with our financial technology platform so all firms have access to the products and services they need to deliver advisory services to their clients." The partnership supports both organizations' commitment to innovation and the responsible application of artificial intelligence. By combining advanced technologies with deep advisory capabilities, Aprio and Intuit aim to help accelerate the evolution of accounting and advisory services and create new value across the business lifecycle.
